fung4.text: U+7E2B 綘 缝 (Mainland simplified) fung4-2 (vernacular rising-tone noun in 裁縫) fung6 (per 《廣韻》扶用切 for noun senses) (F1.59 縫) 裁縫彌縫 (Page 66 #10: (4)縫) To sew, to stitch (Kangxi: 以鍼紩衣也); a seam (Kangxi: 衣縫也), a cleft; _(4)fung (1)(i/)_ (fung4 ji1 縫衣), to sew clothes; _(4)fung (1)san_ (fung4 san1 縫新), to make new clothes; _(4)fung (2)hau_ (fung4 hau2 縫口), a seam; _(4)fung (4)m(a/)i_ (fung4 maai4 縫埋), to sew together. Fan Wan entry: Fixed incomplete strokes in 彌. A gap. 牙縫刷 (ngaa4 fung4 caat3-2): "Interdental brush." 【縫-level】 (bjowng) (_verb-like_) to sew, (_met._) to mend 【縫-departing】 (bjowngH) (_noun-like_) seam

U+9022 (F1.59 逢) 遇也迎也 (Page 66 #9: (4)逢) To meet undesignedly (Kangxi: 遇也, 値也); to meet with; to run against, to occur; great, wide (Kangxi: 大也); _(4)n(a/)n (4)fung_ (naan4 fung4 難逢), difficulty in seeing (as a friend); _(4)fung (4)ying_ (fung4 jing4 逢迎), to go out to meet; _(1)s(e/)ung (4)fung_ (soeng1 fung4 相逢), two persons meeting; _(4)fung (4)yan p(i/)n(6) sh(ut(8) (1)s(a/)m (1)fan w(a/)(6)_ (fung4 jan4 bin6 syut3 saam1 fan1 waa6 逢人便說三分話) speak only a little to strangers; _(4)fung ~~ch(e/)uk(8)~~ ch(e/)uk(9)_ (fung4 zoek6 逢着) to meet one. Williams' 逢迎: Figuratively, to pander to. Williams' 逢着: Corrected _ch(e/)uk(8)_ (zoek3) to _ch(e/)uk(9)_ (zoek6). Every, for all, whenever. To pander to. 【逢-meet】 (bjowng) (_verb-like_) to encounter, to meet (with) (_verb-like_) (_met._) to pander unto (_adjective-like_) large
U+99AE 冯 (Mainland simplified) fung4-2 (vernacular rising-tone for endearment) (F1.59 馮) 姓又音朋 (Page 66 #11: (4)馮) a surname (Kangxi: 姓也).

fung6.text: U+5949 (F1.62 奉) 承也進也又奉侍奉養 (Page 67 #2: 奉(6)) To respectfully receive in both hands, to receive from a superior (Kangxi: 承也 etc.), or offer to him (Kangxi: 與也獻也); to praise, to reverence; _fung(6) ming(6)_ (fung6 ming6 奉命) to receive orders; _sh(i/)(6) fung(6)_ (si6 fung6 侍奉) to cherish one's parents; _fung(6) (4)shing_ (fung6 sing4 奉承), to flatter; _fung(6) ho(6)_ (fung6 ho6 奉賀) to make a congratulatory present; _fung(6) sz'(6)_ (fung6 si6 奉事) to wait upon; _fung(6) hau(6)_ (fung6 hau6 奉候) to offer congratulations. Williams' 奉候: Or, to await respectfully. With both hands, i.e. respectfully. To serve, to provide for. To adhere to. To believe. To carry out. 【奉】 (bjowngX) (_verb-like_) to receive (two-handedly) (_verb-like_) to present (two-handedly) (_verb-like_) to carry (two-handedly), to serve (_verb-like_) (_met._) to carry out (_verb-like_) (_met._) to reverence (_verb-like_) (_met._) to adhere unto

U+9CF3 凤 fung6-2 (vernacular rising-tone noun) (F1.62 鳳) 鳳凰羽虫之長 (Page 67 #3: 鳳(6)) A fabulous bird (Kangxi: 神鳥也 etc.), the male is called _fung(6)_ (fung6 鳳), the female _(4)wong_ (wong4 凰)_;_ the Chinese phoenix; it seems to be derived from the argus pheasant; the empress is poetically called _fung(6)_ (fung6 鳳). Fan Wan entry: Corrected malformed 凰. That 鳳 in the generic "phoenix" sense is considered feminine is because it is contrasted with masculine 龍 "dragon". A surname (Kangxi: 姓). 【鳳】 (bjuwngH) (_noun-like_) male-phoenix The "female prostitute" sense appears to be local to Hong Kong. 【鳳】 (fung6, fung6-2) A female prostitute. 鳳姐 (fung6 ze2): "Prostitute lady." 一樓一鳳 (jat1 lau4 jat1 fung6-2): "One apartment one prostitute." 【鳳爪】 (fung6 zaau2) Chicken feet (as food).

fut3.text: U+95CA 濶 䦢 阔 (Mainland simplified) fut3-2 (rising second in vernacular 闊闊地) (F2.79 濶) 廣也間濶疎濶 (Page 67 #5: 闊(8)) Broad, wide (Kangxi: 廣也), large; ample; distant (Kangxi: 疏也一曰遠也, 闊遠也), separated (Kangxi: 乖闊); liberal; diligent (Kangxi: 契闊勤苦也); to widen, to enlarge, to relax (Kangxi: 寬也); _f(u/)t(8) t(a/)i(6)_ (fut3 daai6 闊大) ample, capacious; _(4)w(a/)ng f(u/)t(8)_ (waang4 fut3 橫闊) broad across; _t(i/)m(6) f(u/)t(8)_ (dim6 fut3 掂闊) across the length; _(1)sho f(u/)t(8)_ (so1 fut3 疏闊) long separated (as friends); _k(a/)n(3) f(u/)t(8)_ (gaan3 fut3 間闊) widely sundered, long separated (Kangxi: 凡久不相見曰閒闊); _f(u/)t(8) lok(9)_ (fut3 lok6 闊落) agreeable, spacious. Fan Wan entry: Corrected ⿰𤴔朿 to 疎. Impractical (Kangxi: 迂闊). Sparse. 【契闊】 (khet khwat) (_adjective-like_) widely separated (_adjective-like_) hard working 【闊】 (khwat) (_adjective-like_) widely separated (_adjective-like_) wide (_verb-like_) to widen, (_met._) to ease Used in 契闊.

gam2.text: U+5649 咁 (Cantonese) (Page 173 #9: (2)噉) An adverb of quality, so, thus, this manner; an interjection of surprise; _(2)k(o\)m ~~(5)y(e/)ung~~ y(e/)ung(6) ts(o\)(6) tak(7)_ (gam2 joeng6-2 zou6 dak1 噉樣做得) this will do, very well; _tsau(6) (2)k(o\)m_ (zau6 gam2 就噉), stop, well; _(2)k(o\)m ~~(5)y(e/)ung~~ y(e/)ung(6) (2)tsz'_ (gam2 joeng6 zi2 噉樣子) such a style! used in depreciation; _(2)k(o\)m w(a/)(6)_ (gam2 waa6 噉話) if you say so, if it be so; _(1)t(')ung (1)t(o\) hai(6) (2)k(o\)m k(e/)(3)_ (tung1 dou1 hai6 gam2 ge3 通都係噉嘅) they are all just so, all alike; _(2)k(o\)m k(e/)(3)! (4)'m (2)h(o\) (2)k(o\)m_ (gam2 ge3-2! m4 hou2 gam2 噉嘅、唔好噉), so! don't do so, that'll not do; _(2)k(o\)m (2)t(a/)m ts(o\)(6)_ (gam2 daam2 zou6 噉膽做) so daring, brave. Even in modern Cantonese, this word is conservatively pronounced kom, not kɐm. See below. Williams' 噉樣做得: Corrected _(5)y(e/)ung_ (joeng5) to _y(e/)ung(6)_ (joeng6-2). Williams' 噉樣子: Corrected _(5)y(e/)ung_ (joeng5) to _y(e/)ung(6)_ (joeng6). A more modern equivalent would be 噉嘅樣 gam2 ge3 joeng6-2. Williams' 噉嘅: This is a rhetorical interrogative, better rendered "like so?" than "so!". Williams' 噉膽做: Better rendered "to do with gall like so". Not the best example with which to demonstrate 噉. 【噉】 (gam2) Like so, like that, in such a manner, this way. 乜你噉㗎 (mat1 nei5 gam2 gaa3): "Why are you like this?" 噉樣 (gam2 joeng6-2): "Like so." 噉嘅樣 (gam2 ge3 joeng6-2): "Looking like that." 爛成噉 (laan6 seng4 gam2): "Broken to such a degree." 就噉 (zau6 gam2): "Leave it at that." 噉點得㗎 (gam2 dim2 dak1 gaa3): "How is this acceptable?" 噉至得𠺢嘛 (gam2 zi3 dak1 ga1 maa3): "Only like so will it be acceptable." 你噉都唔知 (nei5 gam2 dou1 m4 zi1): "How can you not even know a simple thing like that?" 成個乞兒噉 (seng4 go3 hat1 ji4-1 gam2): "Like a complete beggar." 如果你好似狗一樣噉食嘢 (jyu4 gwo2 nei5 hou2 ci5 gau2 jat1 joeng6 gam2 sik6 je5): "If you will eat things in such a manner that is the same as a dog" (see ''Kill Bill: Volume 2''). Used conjunctively. 噉走㗎喇 (gam2 zau2 ga3 laa3): "So then we'll be leaving." 【係噉意】 (hai6 gam2 ji3-2) With barely any effort put in. (Literally, "intention being like so".) 係噉意 (hai6 gam2 ji3-2): "I barely made an effort" (used when presenting someone with a gift). 係噉意揩吓 (hai6 gam2 ji3-2 haai1 haa5): "Brushed against with barely any effort" (i.e. not washed properly). 【係噉先】 (hai6 gam2 sin1) Used to wrap up a conversation. (Literally, "let it be like so at first".) 【就噉】 (zau6 gam2) To leave it at that, to not do any more. The spelling 噉 for gam2 is arbitrary (but well established). The alternative spelling 咁 is also very common. The word 噉 gam2 ("like so") is conservatively pronounced kom, not kɐm. (Arguably, it would be better to romanise the conservative pronunciation as gum2 rather than gam2, but standard Jyutping does not permit this.) Alongside 咁 gam3 ("so/that"), 噉 gam2 ("like so") is one of the few words with a Williams final of _(o\)m_ that has resisted the shift to _am_ in modern Cantonese. Note that 噉 gam2 ("like so") is a *distinct* word from 錦 gam2 (particle of partiality). The latter *cannot* be pronounced kom.

U+9326 𡄎 (for Cantonese particle of partiality) 锦 (Mainland simplified) (F2.37 錦) 五色絲所織 (Page 125 #3: (2)錦) ~~A kind~~ Ornamental work of variegated silk ~~used in ornamental work~~ (Kangxi: 襄色織文也 etc.); embroidered, worked, or knit in colors; elegant, figurative fine writing; flowery, pictured; _~~(1)(i/)~~ (i/)(3) (2)kam_ (ji3 gam2 衣錦), the gentry, official persons; _(2)kam (4)ch(')au_ (gam2 cau4 錦綢), figured pongee; _shap(9) (2)kam (2)(u/)n t(i/)p(9)_ (sap6 gam2 wun2 dip6 什錦碗碟) colored chinaware; _(2)kam sau(3) (4)man_ (gam2 sau3 man4 錦繡文), an elegant style. Williams' "A kind of variegated silk used in ornamental work": This is a poor rendering of both Kangxi 襄色織文也, which defines 錦 as the ornamental work (not the silk), and Fan Wan 五色絲所織, which defines 錦 as 所織 "that weaved" (not the silk). Williams' 衣錦: Corrected _(1)(i/)_ (ji1) to _(i/)(3)_ (ji3). 【錦】 (kimX) (_noun-like_) brocade 【錦】 (gam2) A particle of partial amount. 食錦啲先 (sik6 gam2 di1 sin1): "Eat a bit of it first." 冇錦唿 (mou5 gam2 fat1): "Lost a patch of it." The spelling 錦 is arbitrary. The alternative spelling 𡄎 has poorer font support. The spellings 噉 and 咁 are inadvisable, because 噉 gam2 ("like so") is a distinct word. Unlike 噉 gam2 ("like so"), the particle 錦 gam2 *cannot* be pronounced kom.

gam3.text: U+5481 (Page 173 #10: 咁(3)) An adverb of quantity; so, such; _k(o\)m(3) (5)(un_ (gam3 jyun5 咁遠), so far! _k(o\)m(3) (2)ts(o\)_ (gam3 zou2 咁早), so early! _k(o\)m(3) mat(7) (5)y(e/)_ (gam3 mat1 je5 咁乜嘢), why so? what is the reason? _s(e/)ung(3) ~~mau(6)~~ m(a/)u(6) k(o\)m(3) (2)ch(')au_ (soeng3 maau6 gam3 cau2 相貌咁醜), such an ugly face; _k(o\)m(3) (1)sh(a/) (2)t(a/)m_ (gam3 saa1 daam2 咁沙膽), such great courage; _k(o\)m(3) (1)to_ (gam3 do1 咁多), so many. Even in modern Cantonese, this word is conservatively pronounced kom, not kɐm. See below. Williams' 相貌咁醜: Corrected _mau(6)_ (mau6) to _m(a/)u(6)_ (maau6). 【咁】 (gam3) So, that, to such an extent. 乜你咁蠢㗎 (mat1 nei5 gam3 ceon2 gaa3): "Why are you so stupid?" 得咁多 (dak1 gam3 do1): "There's only that much." 咁晏 (gam3 aan3): "That late in the day?" 咁夜 (gam3 je6): "That late at night?" 咁啱嘅 (gam3 ngaam1 ge3-2): "What a coincidence!" (i.e. fancy seeing you here). 咁誇張 (gam3 kwaa1 zoeng1): "Is it that ridiculous?" 咁得人驚 (gam3 dak1 jan4 geng1): "Is it that frightful?" 冇你咁好氣 (mou5 nei5 gam3 hou2 hei3): "I don't have that good endurance as you" (i.e. I won't persist with you). 【咁上下】 (gam3 soeng6 haa6-2) Roughly that much, roughly to that extent. The spelling 咁 is arbitrary (but well established). The word 咁 gam3 ("so/that") is conservatively pronounced kom, not kɐm. (Arguably, it would be better to romanise the conservative pronunciation as gum3 rather than gam3, but standard Jyutping does not permit this.) Alongside 噉 gam2 ("like so"), 咁 gam3 ("so/that") is one of the few words with a Williams final of _(o\)m_ that has resisted the shift to _am_ in modern Cantonese.

gek1.text: U+4E2E gik1 (alternative) (Page 154 #6: _Kik(7)_ (gik1) _or_ _Kek(7)_ (gek1); here assigned to 丮) A colloquial word; to bind, to take a loop, or tie up with a chain or cord; _kek(7) ch(u(6) (5)k(')(u_ (gek1 zyu6 keoi5 丮住佢) tie it fast, as a boat; _kek(7) (2)keng_ (gek1 geng2 丮頸), to fasten by the neck. The spelling 丮 is arbitrary.

haa1.text: U+54C8 (Page 68 #6: (1)㗿; here corrected to 哈) Laughter; _(1)h(a/) (1)h(a/)_ (haa1 haa1 哈哈), the sound of immoderate laughter. Here, Williams takes 㗿 to be a non-colloquial word (since he gives the Ts(')ing Mandarin reading Hi(a/) under the headword). This is an erroneous reading of the Kangxi entry, as: The laughter-related senses of 㗿 are *not* read _(1)h(a/)_ (haa1); and The sense that *is* read 虛加切 _(1)h(a/)_ (haa1) is explained 與谺同谽谺谷中大空貌. Instead, Williams ought to have acknowledged that _(1)h(a/)_ (haa1) is a colloquial word (though not a Cantonese-specific one).

U+35C7 haa4 (alternative per 《集韻》何加切) (Page 68 #1: (1)㗇) The throat (Kangxi: 咽也); to swallow; (Page 716 #1: (1)㗇) Is also a word of regret, an exclamation of dissatisfaction. 【㗇】 (haa1) An interjection of indignation (usually used before chiding someone with a rhetorical question). 㗇乜你噉㗎 (haa1 mat1 nei5 gam2 gaa3): "How could you be like this?" The spelling 㗇 is arbitrary.
U+7615 (F2.74 瘕) 瘕嗽 (Page 67 #7: (1)瘕) A difficulty in breathing; _(1)h(a/) sau(3)_ (haa1 sau3 瘕嗽) a hacking, a cough; Fan Wan entry: Normalised 𠻳 to 嗽. A throat ailment (Kangxi: 喉病或作疨).

U+8766 㗇 (for Cantonese "bully" sense) 鰕 虾 (Mainland simplified) (F2.74 蝦) 魚蝦 (F2.74 鰕) 同上 (Page 67 #6: (1)蝦(1)鰕) A shrimp, prawn, crawfish (Kangxi 蝦: 與鰕通 etc.); _(1)h(a/) (1)ch(')un_ (haa1 ceon1 蝦膥), ~~crab's eggs~~ shrimp roe; _(1)h(a/) (1)ch(')un ch(a/)p(9)_ (haa1 ceon1 zaap6 蝦膥鈒) a skinflint; _(4)lung (1)h(a/)_ (lung4 haa1 龍蝦), the sea crawfish _(Palinurus);_ _(4)ngan (1)h(a/)_ (ngan4 haa1 銀蝦), sea shrimps; _(4)ming (1)h(a/)_ (ming4 haa1 明蝦), large yellow prawns; _(1)h(a/) k(o\)m(3) (2)ts(a/)n_ (haa1 gam3 zaan2 蝦咁趲), ~~to~~ throwing the arms about passionately; _~~(1)shang~~ (1)sh(a/)ng (1)h(a/) k(o\)m(3) t(')i(u/)(3)_ (saang1 haa1 gam3 tiu3 生蝦咁跳) lively, playful. (Page 68 #1: (1)㗇; here normalised to 蝦) _(1)h(a/) p(a/)(3)_ (haa1 baa3 蝦霸) to insult, to reproach. Williams' 生蝦咁跳: Changed _(1)shang_ (sang1) to vernacular reading _(1)sh(a/)ng_ (saang1). 【蝦】 (haa1) To bully, to pick on. 蝦蝦霸霸 (haa1 haa1 baa3 baa3): "Bullying and tyrannising." 大蝦細 (daai6 haa1 sai3): "Elder picking on younger." 唔准蝦人 (m4 zeon2 haa1 jan4): "No bullying others!" The spelling 蝦 is arbitrary (but well established).

haa4.text: U+8766 蛤 虾 (Mainland simplified) haa1 (common) (Page 67 #6: (1)蝦(1)鰕) The first character (蝦) is also read _(4)h(a/)_ (haa4), as _(4)h(a/) (4)m(a/)_ (haa4 maa4 蝦蟆), a striped frog. Williams' 蝦蟆: Or, a toad. The common reading of 蝦蟆 (usually spelt 蛤蟆) is haa1 mou1; see ''Kung Fu Hustle''. The prescribed reading haa4 maa4 is almost never heard. 【蝦】 (hae) Used in 蝦蟆. 【蝦蟆】 (hae mae) (_noun-like_) frog, toad

haa2.text: U+5413 【吓-interrogative】 (haa2) An initial interrogative particle of doubt, confusion, surprise, disbelief, etc. Similar to initial "Huh?" or "What?" with rising intonation in English. 吓、咁貴 (haa2? gam3 gwai3?): "What? That expensive?" An initial interrogative particle used after not properly hearing something spoken. Similar to initial "Huh?" or "What?" with rising intonation in English, but not considered impolite. 吓 (haa2): "What was that?" A final particle for forming a tag question. 下次我請喇吓 (haa6 ci3 ngo5 ceng2 laa3 haa2): "Next time I'm paying, OK?" The spelling 吓 is arbitrary. Otherwise, a reading variation of 吓 haa5, the "during" suffix after a reduplicated verb.

haa5.text: U+5413 haa5-2 (for Cantonese "during" suffix sense) (Page 67 #12: (5)吓) Once, a time; a while, momentarily; _(2)tang yat(7) (5)h(a/)_ (dang2 jat1 haa5 等一吓), stop a little; _(2)t(a/) yat(7) (5)h(a/)_ (daa2 jat1 haa5 打一吓), strike it once; _(2)k(i/) (5)h(a/)_ (gei2 haa5 幾吓), several times; _yat(7) (5)h(a/) ~~(4)tung~~ (4)t(')ung h(u(3)_ (jat1 haa5 tung4 heoi3 一吓同去) I will go with you soon; _man(6) hau(6) (5)h(a/) (5)k(')(u ~~(2)ch(e/)~~ ch(e/)(3)_ (man6 hau6 haa5 keoi5 ze3 問候吓佢嗻) only came to visit him. Usually spelt 下 for the above senses (i.e. the occurrence classifier and "moment/momentarily" senses). This 下 (haa5) is *not* exclusive to Cantonese; it is the same 下 (haa5) that is present in 一下 (jat1 haa5) and in 一下子 (jat1 haa5 zi2). However, the spelling 下 for this haa5 can be confusing in Cantonese because this 下 is *not* homophonous with 下 (haa6) meaning "down" or "go down". This is especially true in some of Williams' examples, where there is insufficient semantic context to disambiguate between haa5 and haa6 if 下 is used (e.g. 觀吓場 vs 觀下場 under 場 coeng4, and 詳吓 vs 詳下 under 詳 coeng4). Thus, for practical purposes, I have *not* normalised 吓 to 下. However, there are separate haa5 that *are* exclusive to Cantonese; see the Cantonese entry below. Williams' 一吓同去: Corrected _(4)tung_ (dung4) to _(4)t(')ung_ (tung4). Williams' 問候吓佢嗻: Corrected _(2)ch(e/)_ (ze2) to _ch(e/)(3)_ (ze3). In modern Cantonese the final particle would be 啫 ze1 instead of the (now) dated 嗻 ze3. 【吓-modifier】 (haa5) Suffixed after an adjective that has been degree-modified by 幾 "quite". The added suffix somewhat(?) lessens the degree. 今日幾凍吓 (gam1 jat6 gei2 dung3 haa5): "It's quite cold today." 碟餸幾辣吓 (dip6 sung3 gei2 laat6 haa5): "The dish is quite spicy." 【吓-during】 (haa5, haa5-2) Suffixed after a reduplicated verb, before introducing an event that occurs during the action of the verb (i.e. after the action has started but before the action ought to cease). The (tone-unchanged) reading haa5 is strongly preferred when the reduplicated verb is tone 2. 行行吓腳軟 (haang4 haang4 haa5-2 goek3 jyun5): "In the middle of walking I felt weak-legged." 食食吓想嘔 (sik6 sik6 haa5 soeng2 au2): "In the middle of eating I wanted to vomit." 講講吓唔記得咗 (gong2 gong2 haa5 m4 gei3 dak1 zo2): "In the middle of speaking he forgot about it." The spelling 吓 is arbitrary.

haa6.text: U+6687 haa4 (common) (F2.76 暇) 閒逸也 (Page 68 #5: 暇(6)) Leisure, relaxation (Kangxi: 閑也); self-indulgence, unoccupied; _(4)h(a/)n h(a/)(6)_ (haan4 haa6 閒暇) at leisure; _m(i/)(6) h(a/)(6)_ (mei6 haa6 未暇) busy. Carefree. 【暇】 (haeH) (_noun-like_) leisure (_adjective-like_) leisurely, (_met._) carefree

haa4.text: U+7455 瘕 (F2.74 瑕) 玉之玷也 (Page 67 #7: (1)瘕 _(1)H(a/)_ (haa1); here corrected to _(4)H(a/)_ (haa4) and normalised to 瑕) a ~~scar~~ blemish (Kangxi 瘕: 與瑕同); (Page 67 #9: (4)~~？~~瑕) A blemish in a gem (Kangxi 瑕: 玉玷也, 瑕玉之病也); a crack (Kangxi 瑕: 瑕裂也), a flaw; a fault (Kangxi 瑕: 過也), a bad habit; (...), separated (Kangxi 瑕: 相閒曰瑕); _(5)m(i/) yuk(9) (4)m(o\) (4)h(a/)_ (mei5 juk6 mou4 haa4 美玉無瑕), a gem without a flaw, perfect; _(4)h(a/) ~~ts(')z'(3)~~ (1)ts(')z'_ (haa4 ci1 瑕疵) a mistake, carelessness. Williams misprints the headword 瑕 with an additional stroke in the middle component (equivalent to 𩙿 minus 亼); here corrected. Fan Wan entry: Corrected 𪻕 to 玷. Williams' "a crack": Metaphorically, a gap. Williams' 瑕疵: Corrected _ts(')z'(3)_ (ci3) to _(4)ts(')z'_ (ci4) and normalised to _(1)ts(')z'_ (ci1). Emptiness (Kangxi: 瑕謂虛脆也). 【瑕】 (hae) (_noun-like_) blemish, flaw

U+8578 (F2.74 蕸) 芙蕖葉 (Page 716 #2: (4)蕸) The leaves of the water lily (Kangxi: 荷芙蕖, 其葉蕸). Fan Wan entry: Corrected ⿱艹⿱⿰氵臣木 to 蕖, and corrected 藥 to 葉. Williams' "leaves of the water lily": That is, the lotus leaf.

U+9050 徦 瑕 霞 (F2.74 遐) 遠也 (Page 67 #8: (4)遐) Remote, distant, far from (Kangxi: 遠也); why, how; _(4)h(a/) (5)(i/) (1)k(a/)i (1)ch(i/)_ (haa4 ji5 gaai1 zi1 遐邇皆知), it is known by everybody. (Page 67 #9: (4)~~？~~瑕; here normalised to 遐) distant (Kangxi 瑕: 遠也), (...); Long-lasting. 【遐】 (hae) (_adjective-like_) distant, (_met._) lasting (_adverb-like_) how, why

U+971E 赮 (F2.74 霞) 雲霞烟霞 (Page 67 #10: (4)霞) Clouds tinged red (Kangxi: 赤雲氣也 etc., 通作赮); vapor, smokiness; _mok(9) (4)h(a/) m(o\)(6)_ (mok6 haa4 mou6 莫霞霧) don't move about so, be still; _(4)h(a/) p(')(u/)i(3)_ (haa4 pui3 霞珮) a noblewoman's robe. Williams' 霞珮: Whilst 珮 is literally a jade ornament, the rendering as "robe" is correct. See the Cantonese opera 《紫釵記》, which has 戴鳳冠、披霞珮 ("put on the phoenix crown, and drape the sky-red ornamental robe"). Sky-red.

haa5.text: U+4E0B 吓 (Cantonese) (Page 67 #11: (5)下) The reading _(5)h(a/)_ (haa5) is present in Williams, but not with the correct senses. The alternative form 吓 may be more practical in Cantonese. See commentary at 吓 haa5. Classifier for occurrences of a repeatable action. A while, a moment, momentarily.

haa6.text: U+4E0B 丅 haa4 (common in 下巴) haa6-2 (vernacular in 咁上下) (F2.76 下) 上下低也早也降也 (Page 67 #11: (5)下 _(5)H(a/)_ (haa5); here corrected to _H(a/)(6)_ (haa6)) To descend, to come down (Kangxi: 降也自上而下也); _~~(5)h(a/)~~ h(a/)(6) (4)sh(un_ (haa6 syun4 下船) to go aboard; _~~(5)h(a/)~~ h(a/)(6) (4)lau_ (haa6 lau4 下樓), go down stairs; _~~(5)h(a/)~~ h(a/)(6) h(i/)(3)_ (haa6 hei3 下氣) to restrain the temper; _~~(5)h(a/)~~ h(a/)(6) (2)ki(u/)_ (haa6 giu6-2 下轎) to get out of a sedan; _~~(5)h(a/)~~ h(a/)(6) t(a/)n(6)_ (haa6 daan6-2 下蛋) to lay an egg; _~~(5)h(a/)~~ h(a/)(6) t(')(a/)p(8)_ (haa6 taap3 下榻) to lodge; _~~(5)h(a/)~~ h(a/)(6) pat(7)_ (haa6 bat1 下筆) to write; _(1)kwan (4)nang ~~(5)h(a/)~~ h(a/)(6) h(a/)(6)_ (gwan1 nang4 haa6 haa6 君能下下) a sage knows how to condescend; _~~(5)h(a/)~~ h(a/)(6) (2)shau_ (haa6 sau2 下手), to begin to act. (Page 68 #2: 下(6)) Below, down, bottom, inferior (Kangxi: 在下之下對上之稱); mean, vulgar (Kangxi: 賤也); next (Kangxi: 後也); _tsoi(6) (2)tai h(a/)(6)_ (zoi6 dai2 haa6 在底下) it is below; _h(a/)(6) (2)tai_ (haa6 dai2 下底), the bottom, underneath; _h(a/)(6) ~~t(')sz'(3)~~ ts(')z'(3)_ (haa6 ci3 下次) next time; _h(a/)(6) (ut(9)_ (haa6 jyut6 下月) next moon; _h(a/)(6) (4)man_ (haa6 man4 下民), common people; _h(a/)(6) (4)lau_ (haa6 lau4 下流), the lowest classes, lowlive, vicious; _(4)m(o\) h(a/)(6) lok(9)_ (mou4 haa6 lok6 無下落) no fixed business or residence; _h(a/)(6) (5)m(a/) (1)wai_ (haa6 maa5 wai1 下馬威), a humbug; _h(a/)(6) tsok(8)_ (haa6 zok3 下作) to covet, to long for, unscrupulous; _h(a/)(6) ~~(4)p(a/)~~ (4)p(')(a/)_ (haa6 paa4 下巴), the chin; _h(a/)(6) (1)sheng_ (haa6 seng1 下聲), a low sound, or voice; _h(a/)(6) p(i/)n(6)_ (haa6 bin6 下便) the right side, the lower; _h(a/)(6) (4)yan_ (haa6 jan4 下人), official underlings. Fan Wan entry: Corrected ⿰亻氏 to 低. Williams has attempted to distinguish the now (very) obsolete rising-tone reading _(5)h(a/)_ (haa5) from the departing-tone reading _h(a/)(6)_ (haa6), but he has gotten the senses the wrong way round. Classically, it is the positional/directional sense that is rising, and the verb sense that is departing. Williams' 下船: That is, to go down *onto* the boat. Also used to mean the opposite (to go down *from* the boat, i.e. to disembark). Williams' 下底: Less common than 下低. Williams' 下次: Corrected _t(')sz'(3)_ (aspirate in wrong position) to _ts(')z'(3)_. Williams' 下馬威: Here, "humbug" means "fraud" or "sham". This is the meaning when 下馬威 is used sarcastically to mock a (vain) show of authority or might. Williams' 下作: Better rendered as adjectives. Williams' 下巴: Corrected _(4)p(a/)_ (baa4) to _(4)p(')(a/)_ (paa4). 【下-rising】 (haeX) (_adverb-like_) down, downward (_postposition-like_) below, under (_adjective-like_) below, lower, inferior 【下-departing】 (haeH) (_verb-like_) to go down, to alight (_verb-like_) to down, to put down

U+590F 昰 (F2.76 夏) 春夏又大也 (Page 68 #3: 夏(6)) Summer (Kangxi: 四時二曰夏 etc.); a mansion (Kangxi: 大屋曰夏); ~~clear;~~ variegated (Kangxi: 五色曰夏); name of a dynasty from B.C. 2205 to 1766 (Kangxi: 國號禹受舜禪易虞爲夏); _h(a/)(6) (1)t(')(i/)n_ (haa6 tin1 夏天), summer weather; _h(a/)(6) kwai(3)_ (haa6 gwai3 夏季) summer months; _h(a/)(6) p(o\)(3)_ (haa6 bou3 夏布) grasscloth; _H(a/)(6) (4)ch(')i(u/)_ (haa6 ciu4 夏朝), the Hi(a/) dynasty. Fan Wan entry: Corrected 夭 to 大. Williams' "B.C. 2205 to 1766": Per the traditional chronology. An historical appellation for the notion of "civilised China" (Kangxi: 中國曰華夏). The name of a state (Kangxi: 國名). A surname. 【夏-rising】 (haeX) (_adjective-like_) great (_adjective-like_) variegated 【夏-departing】 (haeH) (_noun-like_) summer

U+5EC8 厦 夏 (F2.76 厦) 屋也 (Page 68 #4: 厦(6); here normalised to 廈) A mansion (Kangxi 廈: 大屋), a side room (Kangxi 廈: 今之門廡旁廣而卑); _h(a/)(6) (4)m(u/)n_ (haa6 mun4 廈門), Amoy; _Mong(6) h(a/)(6)_ (mong6 haa6 望廈) the village of W(a/)nghi(a/) near Macao. A house (Kangxi 廈: 屋也). 【廈】 (haeX) (_noun-like_) house, mansion

haai1.text: U+63E9 (F2.25 揩) 虛佳切擦也磨也 (Page 69 #1: (1)揩) To rub, to wipe (Kangxi: 摩拭也); _(1)h(a/)i (1)kon tseng(6)_ (haai1 gon1 zeng6 揩乾淨) wipe shoes clean; _(1)h(a/)i (4)mo_ (haai1 mo4 揩磨), to scour off (as rust); _(1)h(a/)i (4)m(a/)i (4)ts(')(e/)ung_ (haai1 maai4 coeng4 揩埋牆) rub it on the wall; _(5)n(i/) mok(9) (1)h(a/)i (1)ts(')an (5)ngo_ (nei5 mok6 haai1 can1 ngo5 你莫揩嚫我), don't rub against me; _(1)h(a/)i ~~ts(')at(7)~~ ts(')(a/)t(8)_ (haai1 caat3 揩擦) to rub (as with sandpaper). Fan Wan entry: Corrected ⿸虍皿 to 虛, corrected malformed 佳切擦, and fixed missing final stroke in 磨. Williams' 揩擦: Corrected _ts(')at(7)_ (cat1) to _ts(')(a/)t(8)_ (caat3). 【揩】 (haai1) To brush against. 揩到佢架車 (haai1 dou3-2 keoi5 gaa3 ce1): "Brushed against his car." 揩花咗 (haai1 faa1 zo2): "Scratched from being brushed against."

haai4.text: U+56A1 鞋 (for Cantonese "rough" sense) haai4-2 (rising second in vernacular 嚡嚡地) haai5 (rising alternative for interjection) (Page 69 #4: (4)嚡) An exclamation of disappointment, Alas! Oh! rough, hispid, harsh; _lak(9) k(o\)m(3) (4)h(a/)i_ (lak6-1 gam3 haai4 竻咁嚡), sharp as a bramble, morose, surly; _(1)ts(')(o\) (4)h(a/)i_ (cou1 haai4 粗嚡), coarse and rough; _(5)k(')(u sham(6) (4)h(a/)i_ (keoi5 sam6 haai4 佢甚嚡), he's very stingy. 【嚡-interjection】 (haai4, haai5) An interjection of disappointment, complaint, etc. (i.e. a sigh). 【嚡-rough】 (haai4) Rough (of a surface or texture). 煮嚡咗 (zyu2 haai4 zo2): "Cooked it rough" (i.e. overcooked, as opposed to 滑 "smooth"). 【嚡澀澀】 (haai4 saap3 saap3, haai4 saap6 saap6) Rough (of a surface or texture). The spelling 嚡 is arbitrary both for the interjection and for "rough" (which are distinct words). The spelling 澀 in 嚡澀澀 is etymologically sound. However, it should be noted that Williams has 嚡匝匝, taking 匝 _s(a/)p(8)_ (saap3) to be a colloquial word that "when repeated ... is a strong affirmative". See 匝 saap3 (TODO).

U+8AE7 龤 谐 (Mainland simplified) (F2.26 諧) 和也合也 (Page 69 #2: (4)諧) To harmonize, to agree (Kangxi: 詥也); to pair (Kangxi: 耦也); consenting, in concord (Kangxi: 合也調也); of one mind; ~~to laugh~~ laughworthy, humorous (Kangxi: 諧之言皆也辭淺會俗皆悅笑也); _(4)h(a/)i (5)l(o\)_ (haai4 lou5 諧老), an old couple; _(4)wo (4)h(a/)i_ (wo4 haai4 和諧), agreeing (as married people), cordial; _(4)h(a/)i (1)yam_ (haai4 jam1 諧音), a chord. Williams' 和諧: In 21st-century usage, a euphemism for Internet censorship in China. Williams' 諧音: Also near-homophony. 【諧】 (heaj) (_adjective-like_) concordant, resonant

U+978B 𩋔 𩋘 鞵 haai4-2 (vernacular rising-tone noun in 拖鞋) (F2.26 𩋘) 履𩋘 (F2.26 鞋) 同上 (F2.26 鞵) 同上 (Page 69 #3: (4)鞋) A shoe (Kangxi: 鞋解也著時縮其上如履然解其上則舒解也, 本作鞵); _yat(7) t(u/)i(3) (4)h(a/)i_ (jat1 deoi3 haai4 一對鞋), a pair of shoes; _(4)h(a/)i h(un(3)_ (haai4 hyun3 鞋楦) a last; _(1)kung (4)h(a/)i_ (gung1 haai4 弓鞋), a woman's shoe; _(1)t(')o (4)h(a/)i_ (to1 haai4-2 拖鞋), slippers; _(4)h(a/)i (1)kam_ (haai4 gam1 鞋金), fees paid house agents; _(4)h(a/)i pat(9)_ (haai4 bat6 鞋拔) a shoe-horn; _(4)shing (2)tsai (4)h(a/)i_ (sing4-2 zai2 haai4 繩仔鞋), cord sandals; _(2)p(o\) (4)h(a/)i (2)l(o\)_ (bou2 haai4 lou2 補鞋佬) a cobbler; _ch(e/)uk(8) (4)h(a/)i_ (zoek3 haai4 着鞋), to put on shoes. Williams' 弓鞋: Per the practice of foot binding. Williams' 鞋拔: The preferred term for "shoehorn" in Cantonese is 鞋抽. 【鞋】 (hea) (_noun-like_) shoe

haai5.text: U+736C 解 haai6 (recast to departing) (F2.28 獬 _H(a/)i(6)_ (haai6)) 獬豸 (Page 69 #6: (5)獬) A fabulous animal, called _(5)h(a/)i ch(a/)i(6)_ (haai5 zaai6 獬豸) (Kangxi: 獬豸也 etc.), or ~~lion-unicorn~~ unicorn of understanding; embroidered on the robes of censors and judges; haughty, stern. Fan Wan entry: The component 牛 of the headword is printed as 㐄. Williams also prints the component 牛 of the headword as 㐄. 【獬】 (heaX) (_adjective-like_) understanding Used in 獬豸.

U+87F9 蚧 蠏 䲒 (F2.27 蠏) 螃蠏 (F2.27 蟹) 同上 (Page 69 #5: (5)蠏; here normalised to 蟹) A crab (Kangxi 蟹: 蟲名, 仄行蟹屬, 今人謂之旁蠏以其側行故也 etc.); _(5)h(a/)i (1)kang_ (haai5 gang1 蟹羹), crab soup; _(5)h(a/)i (4)k(')(i/)m_ (haai5 kim4 蟹鉗), crab's ~~pincer's~~ pincers; _f(a/)i(3) (5)h(a/)i (5)t(')eng_ (faai3 haai5 teng5 快蟹艇), a boat with many oars; _(1)ch(')(i/) (1)kam (5)h(a/)i_ (ci1 gam1 haai5 黐金蟹), 'a gilded crab,' a rich villain. Fan Wan entry: The component 牛 of the headword is printed as 㐄. Williams also prints the component 牛 of the headword as 㐄. 【蟹】 (heaX) (_noun-like_) crab
U+880F (F2.27 蠏) 螃蠏 (F2.27 蟹) 同上 (Page 69 #5: (5)蠏) Fan Wan entry: The component 牛 of the headword is printed as 㐄. Williams also prints the component 牛 of the headword as 㐄.

haai6.text: U+89E3 haai5 (alternative) (Page 122 #3: 解(3)) Read _h(a/)i(6)_ (haai6), to mean, to intend; _h(a/)i(6) (i/)(3)_ (haai6 ji3 解意) to make motions, as to the dumb; to talk by signs; to guess. This last (解意) is a local phrase. Williams prints the component 牛 as 㐄. To understand (Kangxi: 曉也 etc., 謂曉悟也). A place name (Kangxi: 地名). A surname (Kangxi: 姓). 【解-understand】 (heaX) (_verb-like_) to understand

haai5.text: U+9082 解 迦 haai6 (per 《廣韻》胡懈切) (F2.27 邂) 邂逅不期而會也 (Page 69 #7: (5)邂) Accidentally (Kangxi: 邂逅不期而會也), a pleasant hap; _(5)h(a/)i hau(6)_ (haai5 hau6 邂逅) an unexpected meeting. The reading _(5)h(a/)i_ (haai5) is not unattested for the "carefree" sense (supplemented below); 《集韻》 has the reading 下買切, explained 邂逅解説皃. Fan Wan entry: Fixed third stroke in 會. The component 牛 of the headword is printed as 㐄. Williams also prints the component 牛 of the headword as 㐄. Carefree (Kangxi: 邂逅解悅貌). 【邂】 (heaH) (_adjective-like_) carefree Used in 邂逅. 【邂逅】 (heaH huwH) (_adjective-like_) carefree and pleased

haai6.text: U+61C8 解 gaai3 (per 《廣韻》古隘切) haai5 (uncommon) (F2.28 懈) 怠也倦也 (Page 69 #9: 懈(6)) Remiss, slow, negligent, inattentive (Kangxi: 怠也, 又或作解); _h(a/)i(6) toi(6)_ (haai6 doi6 懈怠) lazy, slow; _h(a/)i(6) to(6)_ (haai6 do6 懈惰) lazy. The reading _h(a/)i(6)_ (haai6) is not unattested, though Kangxi considers it vulgar and erroneous (俗讀匣母非). Fan Wan entry: The component 牛 of the headword is printed as 㐄. Williams also prints the component 牛 of the headword as 㐄. Tired (Fan Wan: 倦也). 【解-lax】 (heaX) (_adjective-like_) lax, remiss (_verb-like_) to laxen

U+68B0 (F2.28 械) 器械機械又桎梏也 (Page 69 #8: 械(6)) Military weapons, as spear, bow, &c. (Kangxi: 一曰器之總名); shackles, fetters (Kangxi: 一曰桎梏也); _(1)k(i/) h(a/)i(6)_ (gei1 haai6 機械) a curious contrivance, the nicer parts of a machine, a craft or art; _(1)ts(')(e/)ung (1)t(o\) h(i/)(3) h(a/)i(6)_ (coeng1 dou1 hei3 haai6 槍刀器械) ~~guns~~ spears, swords, and other arms. Fan Wan entry: Corrected malformed 桎. Williams' 槍刀器械: Unlikely to be "guns" unless the context is the Opium Wars. A utensil, implement, or mechanism. 【械】 (heajH) (_noun-like_) shackle (_noun-like_) weapon (_noun-like_) utensil, mechanism

U+85A4 䪥 (F2.28 薤) 葷菜山上有薤者下有金 (Page 69 #10: 薤(6)) Chives or onions (Kangxi: 薤似韭之菜也), not permitted to be eaten by people who fast. Fan Wan entry: Corrected headword ⿰歹⿳艹非一 to 薤, and corrected malformed 葷 and 菜. 【薤】 (heajH) (_noun-like_) chive

U+9F58 𬹼 (Mainland simplified) (F2.28 齘) 齒相抵也 (Page 69 #11: 齘(6)) To gnash the teeth (Kangxi: 齒相切也), angry (Kangxi: 䫴齘者切齒怒也 etc.); ~~plates in mail arranged like teeth.~~ Fan Wan entry: Corrected ⿰扌氏 to 抵. Williams' "plates in mail arranged like teeth": This is a misreading of Kangxi's example 凡甲衣之欲其無齘也, which should be rendered "For all armour: wearing it, we wish that it have not gnashing". 【齘】 (heajH) (_verb-like_) to gnash

haak1.text: U+8D6B 焃 爀 hak1 (shorter syllable) (F2.33 赫 _Hak(7)_ (hak1)) 明也盛也 (Page 69 #14: 赫(7) _Hak(7)_ (hak1); here normalised to _H(a/)k(7)_ (haak1)) Bright red, splendid, luminous, like a fire or the sun (Kangxi: 火赤貌 etc., 赫赫然盛也, 赫顯也); angry (Kangxi: 赫怒意); to scorch (Kangxi: 赫炙也), to glisten; clever, elegant; _~~hak(7) hak(7)~~ h(a/)k(7) h(a/)k(7)_ (haak1 haak1 赫赫) hot, glorious, effulgent; _(2)h(i/)n ~~hak(7)~~ h(a/)k(7)_ (hin2 haak1 顯赫) a good scholar, talented. Williams' "to scorch": Kangxi has 又《集韻》虛訝切音罅與嚇同《詩大雅》反予來赫《傳》赫炙也《箋》口距人謂之赫《釋文》毛許白反鄭許嫁反莊子所云以梁國嚇我是也 Unravelling this, we have competing interpretations: From the commentary, 赫 is to be read 許白反 _h(a/)k(7)_ (haak1), and means "scorching" or "fieriness". From the lesser-note, 赫 is to be read 許嫁反 _h(a/)(3)_ (haa3) and is being used for 嚇 "menace". Whilst both meanings are reasonable, the departing-tone reading is indefensible because rhyme is being made with 時亦弋獲. Thus, if one is to interpret 赫 as meaning "menace", then it must be read _h(a/)k(8)_ (haak3) and not _h(a/)(3)_ (haa3). A surname (Kangxi: 姓). Used in 赫連 (a compound surname) (Kangxi: 赫連氏複姓). 【赫】 (xaek) (_adjective-like_) fiery-red, fiery (_adjective-like_) (_met._) resplendent (_verb-like_) (_met._) to resplend

hak1.text: U+8D6B (F2.33 赫) 明也盛也 (Page 69 #14: 赫(7))

haak3.text: U+5580 䘔 kaak1 (alternative) kaak3 (alternative) (_onomatopoeia_) The sound of retching or coughing up (Kangxi: 吐聲 etc.). 喀痰 (kaak1 taam4): "Cough up phlegm."

haak6.text: U+5580 嗄 (Cantonese) 【喀】 (haak6) An interjection of acknowledgement. The spelling 喀 is arbitrary.

haak3.text: U+5687 哧 赫 吓 (Mainland simplified) haa3 (alternative per 《集韻》虚訝切) (F2.90 嚇) 恐嚇驚嚇 (Page 70 #2: 嚇(8)) An angry ~~tone~~ sound (Kangxi: 怒其聲); to threaten, to intimidate; to anger; scared, frightened; _h(a/)k(8) (5)ngo yat(7) t(')i(u/)(3)_ (haak3 ngo5 jat1 tiu3 嚇我一跳) scared me much; _h(a/)k(8) (1)keng_ (haak3 geng1 嚇驚), terrified; _h(a/)k(8) (1)ts(')an_ (haak3 can1 嚇嚫), sick from fright; _h(a/)k(8) ch(a/)(3)_ (haak3 zaa3 嚇詐) to alarm by threats; _h(a/)k(8) shai(3)_ (haak3 sai3 嚇勢) a humbug; _(2)hung h(a/)k(8)_ (hung2 haak3 恐嚇) to idly arouse one's fears. Fan Wan entry: Fixed incomplete and missing strokes in 恐 and 驚. To defy verbally (Kangxi: 口拒人謂之赫, 赫亦作嚇). 【嚇】 (xaek, xaeH) (_verb-like_) to frighten (_verb-like_) to menace

U+5BA2 (F2.90 客) 旅客又寄居曰客 (Page 70 #1: 客(8)) A guest, a visitor (Kangxi: 賔客), a friend; a dealer, customer, a stranger (Kangxi: 凡自外至者皆曰客); foreign; squatters, marauders (Kangxi: 外寇亦曰客); to lodge (Kangxi: 寄也); _(4)yan h(a/)k(8)_ (jan4 haak3 人客) a visitor; _(1)sai h(a/)k(8)_ (sai1 haak3 西客) traders from Shens(i/) (陝西) and Sh(a/)ns(i/) (山西); _~~h(a/)k,~~ h(a/)k(8) t(i/)(6)_ (haak3 dei6 客地) a trading-place; _h(a/)k(8) (4)fong_ (haak3 fong4-2 客房), guest-chamber; _h(a/)k(8) fo(3)_ (haak3 fo3 客貨) inferior goods; _(4)ch(')(a/) h(a/)k(8)_ (caa4 haak3 茶客) teamen; _h(a/)k(8) sui(3)_ (haak3 seoi3 客歲) last year; _h(a/)k(8) (1)ping_ (haak3 bing1 客兵), foreign troops; _(1)f(a/)n h(a/)k(8)_ (faan1 haak3 番客) a foreigner; _h(a/)k(8) (1)ts(')ai_ (haak3 cai1 客妻), a whore; _h(a/)k(8) (1)k(a/) (4)yan_ (haak3 gaa1 jan4 客家人), people from Ki(a/)ying chau (嘉應州); _h(a/)k(8) t(')(o\)(3)_ (haak3 tou3 客套) to flatter a guest; _(2)h(o\) h(a/)k(8) (4)ts(')ing_ (hou2 haak3 cing4 好客情), a cordial reception; _(4)t(')ong h(a/)k(8)_ (tong4 haak3 堂客) a lady visitor. Fan Wan entry: Normalised ⿱宀竒 to 寄. Williams' 客地: Corrected comma to tone marker _(8)_ for 客. In modern usage, used in 客觀 "objective" (in contrast with 主觀 "subjective"). A retainer, a person retained (i.e. employment) by a lord. 食客 (sik6 haak3): "Eating guest" (i.e. one who eats from being retained as a guest by a lord). A noun-forming suffix used to denote engagement in an activity. 政客 (zing3 haak3): "Politician." 刺客 (ci3 haak3): "Assassin." 劍客 (gim3 haak3): "Swordsman." 海客 (hoi2 haak3): "Mariner." 【客】 (khaek) (_noun-like_) guest

haam2.text: U+9921 May appear with radical component 𩙿 or 飠 (assumed here), depending on the font.

haam6.text: U+9921 May appear with radical component 𩙿 or 飠 (assumed here), depending on the font. 膁 䭑 馅 (Mainland simplified) haam6-2 (vernacular rising-tone noun) (F2.65 餡) 餅中之物 (Page 71 #5: 餡(6)) ~~Small flour cakes, like dumplings, with meat or fruit inside~~ The filling within flour cakes, dumplings, &c. (Kangxi: 凡米麫食物坎其中實以雜味曰餡或作䭑); _~~(2)p(a/)u~~ (1)p(a/)u h(a/)m(6)_ (baau1 haam6-2 包餡) pastry ~~cakes~~ cake filling; _(4)wan (1)t(')an h(a/)m(6)_ (wan4 tan1 haam6-2 雲吞餡) the filling of pork dumplings cooked in sugar. The original departing reading haam6 is almost never heard, having been supplanted by vernacular rising haam6-2. Fan Wan entry: Corrected headword ⿰𩙿⿱⺈曰 to 餡, and corrected 𢪱 to 物. Williams' "Small flour cakes, like dumplings, ...": This is a misreading of Kangxi's definition. 餡 refers to the filling, not to the entire bun or dumpling. Williams' 包餡: Corrected _(2)p(a/)u_ (baau2) to _(1)p(a/)u_ (baau1). Williams' 雲吞餡: Evidently different from the modern wonton, which is not cooked in sugar.

haam3.text: U+558A 嚂 㘕 haam2 (per 《廣韻》呼覽切 and 呼豏切) haam5 (per 《廣韻》下斬切) (F2.64 喊) 譁聲 (Page 71 #3: 喊(3)) To call, to halloo after, to call for, to vociferate (Kangxi 嚂: 聲也亦與喊同); a call (Kangxi: 喊聲也); to cry, to bawl; angry cries (Kangxi: 怒聲); _h(a/)m(3) (5)k(')(u_ (haam3 keoi5 喊佢) call him; _t(a/)i(6) (1)sheng h(a/)m(3)_ (daai6 seng1 haam3 大聲喊) to call aloud, to cry out; _h(a/)m(3) huk(7)_ (haam3 huk1 喊哭) to cry; _(2)t(a/) h(a/)m(3) l(o\)(6)_ (daa2 haam3 lou6 打喊露) to gape; _h(a/)m(3) (1)t(')ung t(')au(3)_ (haam3 tung1 tau3 喊通透) to cry it out; _h(a/)m(3) sh(a/)t(8) (4)l(i/)n (1)t(')(i/)n_ (haam3 saat3 lin4 tin1 喊殺連天), the noise of battle cries reaches to heaven; _h(a/)m(3) (1)sheng t(a/)i(6) k(e/)(3)_ (haam3 seng1 daai6 ge3 喊聲大嘅) useless regrets; _h(a/)m(3) kau(3)_ (haam3 gau3 喊救) to call upon to save. Williams' 打喊露: Better rendered "to yawn". 【嚂】 (xamX) (_verb-like_) to cry (out) 【打喊露】 (daa2 haam3 lou6) To yawn. 【喊】 (haam3) To cry, to shed tears.

haam4.text: U+51FD May appear with central component 丂 or 了 (assumed here), depending on the font. This extends to all characters containing 函 as a component. 凾 圅 椷 (for "contain" sense) 䤴 (for "armour" sense) 䥁 (for "armour" sense) ham4 (per 《廣韻》胡男切 for "contain" sense) (F2.63 函) 包也容也 (Page 70 #8: (4)函) To contain, to infold, to comprehend in, to envelop (Kangxi: 容也, 函包也, 讀與含同); a letter, or what is contained in an envelop (Kangxi: 書也); liberal, capacious; _(1)p(a/)u (4)h(a/)m_ (baau1 haam4 包函), to keep close, not to utter; _(1)sh(u (4)h(a/)m_ (syu1 haam4 書函), a letter; _(1)ts(un (4)h(a/)m_ (zyun1 haam4 尊函), your favor; _(4)h(a/)m ch(e/)ung(6)_ (haam4 zoeng6 函丈) a teacher ~~or sage's desk~~; _(4)h(a/)m (4)yung_ (haam4 jung4 函容), patiently. The "contain" sense is probably cognate with 含. Fan Wan entry: Fixed missing second stroke in 容. Williams' 尊函: Here, "favor" means "letter". Williams' 函丈: Not a teacher's desk, but a teacher, from the distance prescribed by the Record of Rites, 席間函丈 "between the mats there shall be contained a measure". In modern usage, used in 函數 "function" in mathematics. Armour (Kangxi: 鎧也). 【函】 (hom) (_verb-like_) to contain (_noun-like_) container, (_met._) armour

U+54B8 (F2.63 咸) 皆也又交感也 (Page 70 #5: (4)咸) All, jointly, altogether (Kangxi: 皆也, 悉也); completely, totally; always, all round, reaching everywhere (Kangxi: 咸徧也); concord (Kangxi: 咸同也), associated; ~~hasty;~~ a diagram (Kangxi: 卦名); _pat(7) (4)h(a/)m_ (bat1 haam4 不咸), disagreeing; _(4)H(a/)m (1)fung_ (haam4 fung1 咸豐), the style of the present emperor; _m(a/)n(6) kwok(8) (4)h(a/)m (4)ning_ (maan6 gwok3 haam4 ning4 萬國咸寧), all countries at peace. Fan Wan entry: Corrected ⿳一八夂 to 交, and fixed incompletely printed stroke in 感. Williams' "hasty": Kangxi has 《易雜卦》咸速也. This should not be taken as a definition of 咸. Williams' 咸豐: See the term 咸豐年 below. A surname (Kangxi: 姓). 【咸】 (heam) (_adverb-like_) all, completely, together (_verb-like_) to unite 【咸豐年】 (haam4 fung1 nin4) Ages ago. Note that Emperor Hien-fung (咸豐) reigned from 1850 to 1861, and died at the age of just 30.
U+5563 May appear with 𦈢 having 6 strokes (+8) or 7 strokes (+9 assumed here). (F2.63 啣) 口中物 (F2.63 銜) 馬勒也又口含物曰銜又官之階位曰銜 Fan Wan entry: Corrected both occurrences of 𢪱 to 物, and corrected 舍 to 含.

U+3605 (F2.63 啣) 口中物 (F2.63 銜) 馬勒也又口含物曰銜又官之階位曰銜 (Page 71 #2: (4)？(4)㘅) Fan Wan entry: Corrected both occurrences of 𢪱 to 物, and corrected 舍 to 含. Williams prints the first mouth-radical headword as ⿰口䣃 (rather than 啣). A different character, 𠷢, appears on Page 748 in the character index.
U+3B80 㮭 (F2.63 㮀) 植也 (Page 70 #10: (4)㮀) The Fan Wan says, to plant, to set out (Fan Wan: 植也);
U+6937 㮀 㮭 (Page 70 #10: (4)㮀; here normalised to 椷) but K(a/)ngh(i/) (康熙) defines it a wooden ~~bowl~~ cup (Kangxi 椷: 杯也 etc.).

U+6DB5 ham4 (per 《廣韻》胡男切) ham6 (per 《廣韻》胡感切 for "boat-leak" sense) (F2.63 涵) 水澤涵濡 (Page 70 #9: (4)涵) Submerged (Kangxi: 涵沉也); to leak (Kangxi: 一曰水入船); ~~marshy;~~ to soak; to contain (Kangxi: 容也), capacious; _(4)h(a/)m ~~(4)(un~~ (5)(un_ (haam4 jyun5 涵軟), to soak soft; _(4)h(a/)m (5)y(e/)ung_ (haam4 joeng5 涵養), kindly, to keep one's temper; _(2)shui (4)h(a/)m_ (seoi2 haam4 水涵) a sewer. The reading _(4)h(a/)m_ (haam4) is not unattested; 《集韻》 has the reading 胡讒切, explained 同也詩僭始既涵鄭康成讀. I fail to see why the "contain" sense of 涵 is not considered the same word as 函 (which is probably cognate with 含). Fan Wan entry: Fixed missing strokes in 濡. Williams' "marshy": This is a misreading of Kangxi 水澤多也. Here, 澤 means "moistened". Williams' 涵軟: Corrected _(4)(un_ (jyun4) to _(5)(un_ (jyun5). Well-moistened (Kangxi: 水澤多也). 【涵】 (hom) (_verb-like_) to contain (_adjective-like_) well-moistened, well-soaked

U+8AF4 咸 (F2.63 諴) 和也誠也 (Page 70 #7: (4)諴) Union, harmony (Kangxi: 和也); to be accordant, united; sincere, cordial, hearty (Kangxi: 誠也, 誠感物曰諴). 【諴】 (heam) (_verb-like_) to unite (_noun-like_) unity, (_met._) sincerity

U+929C 啣 㗸 㘅 䘖 衘 衔 (Mainland simplified) (F2.63 啣) 口中物 (F2.63 銜) 馬勒也又口含物曰銜又官之階位曰銜 (Page 71 #1: (4)銜) Bit of a bridle (Kangxi: 馬勒口中, 馬銜所以制之行也); to hold in the mouth (Kangxi: 凡口含物曰銜); to contain; to control one's self, to guide, to order; ~~affected by;~~ ~~moved~~ thankful (Kangxi: 感也), ~~indignant~~ resentful (Kangxi: 憾也); rank (Kangxi: 官吏階位曰銜); _(2)hau (4)h(a/)m muk(9) (2)l(a/)m_ (hau2 haam4 muk6 laam5-2 口銜木欖), to keep silence; _(4)h(a/)m (4)m(u/)i_ (haam4 mui4 銜枚), to hold a bit, to be still; _(1)k(u/)n (4)h(a/)m_ (gun1 haam4 官銜) or _chik(7) (4)h(a/)m_ (zik1 haam4 職銜), an official title; _(4)h(a/)m han(6)_ (haam4 han6 銜恨) to restrain one's indignation. (Page 71 #2: (4)？(4)㘅; here normalised to 銜) To hold in the mouth; used for the preceding (銜) (Kangxi 㘅: 同銜); to receive (as an order); _(4)h(a/)m (4)w(a/)n_ (haam4 waan4 銜環), to hold a gem in the bill, _met._ to requite a kindness; _(4)h(a/)m t(')(i/)t(8) ~~(4)t(')(a/)n~~ t(a/)n(6)_ (haam4 tit3 daan6-2 銜鐵彈), to hold an iron shot in the mouth (punishment of liars in hell); _(4)h(a/)m p(o\)(3)_ (haam4 bou3 銜報) to requite; _(4)h(a/)m ~~meng(6)~~ ming(6)_ (haam4 ming6 銜命) received your orders (said of a friend's request); _(4)h(a/)m ch(u(6) (4)t(')ong (2)l(a/)m_ (haam4 zyu6 tong4 laam5-2 銜住糖欖) sucking a sugared olive, _met._ pleased and silent. Fan Wan entry: Corrected both occurrences of 𢪱 to 物, and corrected 舍 to 含. Williams prints the first mouth-radical headword as ⿰口䣃 (rather than 啣). Yet another form, 𠷢, appears on Page 748 in the character index. Williams' 銜鐵彈: Corrected _(4)t(')(a/)n_ (taan4) to _t(a/)n(6)_ (daan6-2). Williams' 銜命: Corrected _meng(6)_ (meng6) to _ming(6)_ (ming6). To carry (out) (Kangxi: 奉君命而行曰銜命). To connect. 【銜】 (haem) (_noun-like_) bit (_verb-like_) to carry in the mouth, to carry

U+9E79 咸 醎 haam4-2 (rising second in vernacular 鹹鹹地) (F2.63 鹹) 鹽味不淡也 (F2.63 醎) 同上 (Page 70 #6: (4)鹹) ~~Saltish, like sea-water~~ Salty (Kangxi: 北方味也, 不淡, 鹽味); salted, preserved in brine; _(4)h(a/)m shap(7)_ (haam4 sap1 鹹濕) salacious; _(4)h(a/)m ts(')oi(3)_ (haam4 coi3 鹹菜) sour-krout; _(4)h(a/)m (4)t(')(o\)_ (haam4 tou4-2 鹹桃), salted peaches. (Page 716 #3: (4)鹹) In a figurative sense, bitter, distressing, hard to bear; _shau(6) kw(a/)n(3) (4)h(a/)m (2)f(u/)_ (sau6 gwaan3 haam4 fu2 受慣鹹苦), he has long been used to hardships. Fan Wan entry: Corrected 巳 to 口 in the component 咸 of headwords 鹹 and 醎, and corrected malformed 鹽 and 淡. 【鹹】 (heam) (_adjective-like_) salty 【鹹】 (haam4) Lewd, pornographic, erotic. 鹹片 (haam4 pin3-2): "Pornographic video." 【鹹濕】 (haam4 sap1) Lewd, pornographic, erotic. 好鹹濕 (hou2 haam4 sap1): "Very lewd" (or erotic). 鹹濕鬼 (haam4 sap1 gwai2): "Pervert."

haam6.text: U+9677 (F2.65 陷) 坑也阱也險也害也 (Page 71 #4: 陷(6)) Fan Wan entry: Corrected headword ⿰阝⿱⺈曰 to 陷, and normalised semi-simplified 險 to 險.

haan1.text: U+6173 悭 (Mainland simplified) (F2.67 慳) 香閒切吝嗇也 (Page 72 #1: (1)慳) Saving, niggardly, stingy; to be sparing of; _(1)h(a/)n k(i/)m(6)_ (haan1 gim6 慳儉) parsimonious, close; _(1)h(a/)n lun(6)_ (haan1 leon6 慳吝) ~~(or _nun(6)_ (neon6))~~ stingy; _(1)h(a/)n lik(9)_ (haan1 lik6 慳力) saving of strength; _(2)h(o\) (1)h(a/)n_ (hou2 haan1 好慳), closefisted; _(1)h(a/)n (1)f(a/)n_ (haan1 faan1 慳返), saved the expense, spared the trouble. In Cantonese, 慳 is usually used positively to mean "frugal" rather than "stingy" (e.g. in the compliment 知慳識儉). 【慳】 (haan1) To be frugal, to economise. 慳水 (haan1 seoi2): "Save water." 慳錢 (haan1 cin4-2): "Save money." 慳皮 (haan1 pei4-2): "Be frugal." 慳電膽 (haan1 din6 daam2): "Energy-saving light-bulb" (i.e. a compact fluorescent lamp).

haan4.text: U+5AFA 嫻 𡢃 閑 (for "adept" sense) 閒 (for "adept" sense) 娴 (Mainland simplified) (F2.68 嫺) 習熟也雅也 (Page 72 #5: (4)嫺) Accustomed (Kangxi: 習也, 通作閒); ~~loving leisure;~~ elegant (Kangxi: 雅也); _(4)h(a/)n shuk(9)_ (haan4 suk6 嫺熟) accomplished, skilled~~,~~ in; _(4)h(a/)n (5)ng(a/)_ (haan4 ngaa5 嫺雅), apt, polished. Fan Wan entry: Fixed missing and complete strokes in 習 and 雅.
U+61AA (F2.68 憪) 淨也 (Page 72 #4: (4)憪) (...), pleased (Kangxi 憪: 愉也); composed, tranquil, contented (Kangxi 憪: 心靜也); Fan Wan entry: 淨 is likely a typo for 靜.

haan5.text: U+61AA haan6 (recast to departing) (Page 72 #4: (4)憪 _(4)H(a/)n_ (haan4); here corrected to _(5)H(a/)n_ (haan5)) Liberal (Kangxi 憪: 寬大貌), (...); aroused, anxious (Kangxi 憪: 不安貌) ~~for others~~. Furious (Kangxi 憪: 勁忿貌).

haan4.text: U+7647 癎 瞯 𤺛 痫 (Mainland simplified) gaan2 (uncommon) (F2.68 癎) 顚病 (F2.68 𤺛) 同上 (Page 72 #6: (4)癇) Convulsions in children (Kangxi: 病也, 小兒瘨病 etc.); spasms from fright; epilepsy; vulgarly called _f(a/)t(8) (4)y(e/)ung ti(u/)(3)_ (faat3 joeng4 diu3 發羊吊).

U+77AF 瞷 (Page 72 #9: (4)瞯) ~~spots in the eyes;~~ the whites of the eyes showing (Kangxi: 人目多白也) ~~in convulsions~~ from looking up (Kangxi: 戴目也) or askew (Kangxi: 眄也). Williams' "in convulsions": This is a misreading of Kangxi 瞯小兒癇病也, which is an implicit statement that 瞯 is an alternative form of 癇.

U+9591 闲 (Mainland simplified) (F2.68 閑) 闌也止防也又散也習也 (Page 72 #3: (4)閑) A bar or barrier, a fence (Kangxi: 闌也 etc., 閑與梐枑皆禁衞之物也); an inclosure; a fold or stable for horses (Kangxi: 馬闌也 etc.); to close, to obstruct (Kangxi: 閑閡也, 閑遮也); to protect or to guard against (Kangxi: 防也禦也法也); to regulate by law, to forbid; to move about (Kangxi: 閑閑動搖也); large (Kangxi: 大也); accustomed, practiced (Kangxi: 習也); _(4)h(a/)n (2)cho_ (haan4 zo2 閑阻), to embarrass; _(4)h(a/)n ts(a/)p(9)_ (haan4 zaap6 閑習) broken in, used to. Fan Wan entry: Fixed missing strokes in 闌 and 習, and normalised 㪚 to 散. Williams' "embarrass": In the (now) archaic sense of "impede", "obstruct". 【閑】 (hean) (_noun-like_) guardrail (_noun-like_) enclosure (_verb-like_) to guard (against) (_adjective-like_) great (_adjective-like_) well-trained

U+9592 閑 間 闲 (Mainland simplified) haan4-2 (rising second in vernacular 閒閒地) (F2.68 閒) 暇也安逸也 (Page 72 #2: (4)閒) Repose (Kangxi: 安也), leisure (Kangxi: 𨻶也, ...空閒...); indolent; unoccupied, empty; _tak(7) (4)h(a/)n_ (dak1 haan4 得閒), at leisure; _(4)m(o\) (4)h(a/)n_ (mou4 haan4 無閒), busy; _(4)h(a/)n (4)yau_ (haan4 jau4 閒遊), sauntering about; _(4)h(a/)n (2)shau_ (haan4 sau2 閒手), an idler; _(4)h(a/)n w(a/)(6)_ (haan4 waa6-2 閒話) small talk; _(4)h(a/)n sz'(6)_ (haan4 si6 閒事) private, trifling affairs; _(4)yau (2)shau h(o\)(3) (4)h(a/)n_ (jau4 sau2 hou3 haan4 遊手好閒), a vagrant loves leisure; _(4)h(a/)n uk(7)_ (haan4 uk1 閒屋) an untenanted house; _(4)h(a/)n t(i/)(6)_ (haan4 dei6 閒地)) a void place, room; _(1)ch(')au (4)h(a/)n_ (cau1 haan4 抽閒), to take time for; _(4)fong (4)h(a/)n_ (fong4 haan4 防閒), to look out for idlers. (Page 72 #3: (4)閑) Often used for the preceding (閒). Irrelevant. 閒人免進 (haan4 jan4 min5 zeon3): "Irrelevant persons shall avoid proceeding" (i.e. no unauthorised entry). Ordinary. 閒日 (haan4 jat6-2): "Ordinary day" (i.e. weekday). 【閒-voiced】 (hean) (_noun-like_) idle-time (_adjective-like_) idle, idling (_verb-like_) (_met._) to calm 【閒閒地】 (haan4 haan4-2 dei6-2) Used to indicate the lower end of expenditure, time required, etc. (Literally, "even ordinarily".) 閒閒地都要廿蚊 (haan4 haan4-2 dei6-2 dou1 jiu3 jaa6 man1): "Even at the lower end, you'd need to pay twenty bucks."

U+9DF3 鷴 鷼 鹇 (Mainland simplified) (F2.68 鷴) 白鷴鳥名 (Page 72 #7: (4)鷳) A kind of pheasant; _p(a/)k(9) (4)h(a/)n_ (baak6 haan4 白鷳), the silver pheasant (Kangxi: 白鷴鳥名). Fan Wan entry: Corrected two slashes to 灬 in the component 鳥 of the headword.
U+9DF4 (F2.68 鷴) 白鷴鳥名 Fan Wan entry: Corrected two slashes to 灬 in the component 鳥 of the headword.

haan5.text: U+50E9 (F2.69 僩 _(2)H(a/)n_ (haan2)) 香板切武毅貌 (Page 72 #8: (4)僩 _(4)H(a/)n_ (haan4); here corrected to _(5)H(a/)n_ (haan5)) ~~depending on one's-self;~~ liberal, magnanimous (Kangxi: 寬大也). 【僩】 (haenX) (_adjective-like_) magnanimous

U+648A 僩 憪 (for "furious" sense) 𢵧 gaan2 (per 《集韻》賈限切 for "fierce" and "formidable" senses) haan6 (recast to departing) (Page 72 #8: (4)僩 _(4)H(a/)n_ (haan4); here corrected to _(5)H(a/)n_ (haan5) and normalised to 撊) Courageous; martial (Kangxi 僩: 武貌); formidable, brave; Furious (Kangxi 撊: 勁忿貌). Fierce (Kangxi 僩: 晉魏閒謂猛爲僩). 【撊】 (haenX, keanX) (_adjective-like_) furious, fierce, (_met._) formidable

haan6.text: U+9650 䦘 (for "doorsill" sense) 𨵬 (for "doorsill" sense) (F2.71 限) 門限界限又度也阻也 (Page 72 #10: 限(6)) To limit, to fix or set a time, to assign, to adjust; to impede, to moderate; a limit (Kangxi: 度也), impediment (Kangxi: 阻也), boundary (Kangxi: 界也), restriction; a few, a short time; a threshold (Kangxi: 一曰門榍也, 閾也, 與䦘通門閾也); _(4)m(o\) h(a/)n(6)_ (mou4 haan6 無限) illimitable; _(4)ho h(a/)n(6)_ (ho4 haan6 何限) what limit, endless, numberless; _(5)yau h(a/)n(6)_ (jau5 haan6 有限) a few, limited; _h(a/)n(6) (2)k(i/) ~~yat(7)~~ yat(9)_ (haan6 gei2 jat6 限幾日) how many days do you set? _~~kwo(6)~~ kwo(3) h(a/)n(6)_ (gwo3 haan6 過限) overpast the time; _(1)f(u/)n h(a/)n(6)_ (fun1 haan6 寬限) to extend the time; _h(a/)n(6) ~~teng(6)~~ ting(6)_ (haan6 ding6 限定) exactly so many; _h(a/)n(6) t(o\)(6)_ (haan6 dou6 限度) a ~~fixed~~ limited measure. (Page 72 #11: ~~閬~~𨵬(6)) The threshold of a door (Kangxi 𨵬: 門𨵬也本作限俗加門作𨵬). (Page 716 #4: 閬(6)) Should be changed to 𨵬; the first (閬) is read _(4)long_ (long4). 【限】 (heanX) (_noun-like_) barrier, limit

haang1.text: U+5751 坈 阬 (F2.88 坑) 坑坎阱也 (Page 74 #5: (1)坑) A ditch, trench, hollow, hole, cave, or pit, natural or artificial (Kangxi: 同阬, 虛也, 陷也); the furrows in a roof; a pit to entrap wild beasts; to throw into a pit; to excavate; _(1)h(a/)ng (4)k(')(u_ (haang1 keoi4 坑渠), a sewer or drain; _(1)h(a/)ng (2)h(o\)m_ (haang1 ham2 坑坎), a natural gully, a ravine; _~~(2)L(o\)~~ (5)L(o\) (1)h(a/)ng_ (lou5 haang1 老坑), a quarry in ~~Sh(a/)uking~~ Ch(a/)uking f(u/) (肇慶府) which furnishes good inkstones; _(2)shui (1)h(a/)ng (4)m(u/)n_ (seoi2 haang1 mun4 水坑門), a sluice; _(4)m(u/)i (1)h(a/)ng_ (mui4 haang1 煤坑), a coal pit. Williams' 老坑: Corrected _(2)L(o\)_ (lou2) to _(5)L(o\)_ (lou5). 【阬】 (khaeng) (_noun-like_) pit (_verb-like_) (_met._) to bury

hang4.text: U+6841 haang4 (longer syllable) (F2.88 桁 _(4)H(a/)ng_ (haang4)) 屋上桁槁 (Page 74 #6: (4)桁 _(4)H(a/)ng_ (haang4); here normalised to _(4)Hang_ (hang4)) The purlines of a roof (Kangxi: 屋桁屋橫木也); _~~(4)h(a/)ng~~ (4)hang kok(8)_ (hang4 gok3 桁桷) purlines and rafters; _uk(7) ~~(4)h(a/)ng~~ (4)hang_ (uk1 hang4 屋桁), purlines. A wooden lid for sacrificial wine jars used in burial (Kangxi: 葬具, ...所以蓋也苞筲甕甒之屬以木桁塞其口也). 【桁】 (haeng) (_noun-like_) wooden-lid

U+884C 恆 (for Cantonese "taut/maximally" sense) 恒 (for Cantonese "taut/maximally" sense) 衡 (for Cantonese "taut/maximally" sense) haang4 (vernacular longer syllable for "walk" and "move" senses) hang4-2 (rising second in vernacular 行行地) (F2.30 行) 行步踐也履也 (Page 73 before #1: (4)行) (This character (行) is often pronounced like the next syllable (haang).) (Page 73 #1: (4)行) To go, to walk, to proceed (Kangxi: 人之步趨也, 適也往也去也); to act, to do, to direct; imports the action of the following verb; to appeal, or transfer a case; a step; a road (Kangxi: 路也), a way (Kangxi: 道也), a path; one of the elements (Kangxi: 五行 etc.); a manner; motion; _~~(4)hang~~ (4)h(a/)ng l(o\)(6)_ (haang4 lou6 行路) to walk in the way; _p(o\)(6) (4)hang_ (bou6 hang4 步行), to travel afoot; _(4)hang (4)yan_ (hang4 jan4 行人), a traveler; _~~(4)hang~~ (4)h(a/)ng (5)lai_ (haang4 lai5 行禮), to visit, to attend to prescribed rites; _(4)hang (5)(u_ (hang4 jyu5 行語), to tell to; _(4)hang (5)l(i/)_ (hang4 lei5 行李), baggage; _(5)'ng (4)hang_ (ng5 hang4 五行), the 5 elements; _(4)hang k(a/)u(3)_ (hang4 gaau3 行教) to promulgate; _t(a/)i(6) (4)hang_ (daai6 hang4 大行), the recently deceased emperor or empress; _~~(4)hang~~ (4)h(a/)ng (4)t(')au_ (haang4 tau4 行頭), head-gear, masks, &c., used by actors; _(4)hang (1)h(e/)ung_ (hang4 hoeng1 行香), to go in procession; _(4)hang (1)ts(')ing_ (hang4 cing1 行清), to worship at the tombs in spring; _(4)hang (4)ying_ (hang4 jing4 行刑), to punish; _~~(4)hang~~ (4)h(a/)ng (1)ts(')(i/)n p(o\)(6)_ (haang4 cin1 bou6 行千步) to 'walk a mile;' _~~(4)hang~~ (4)h(a/)ng (4)sh(un_ (haang4 syun4-2 行船), to weigh anchor, to follow the sea, to act as a sailor; _~~(1)hang~~ (4)h(a/)ng (4)m(a/)i tik(7)_ (haang4 maai4 dik1 行埋滴) step aside a little! _(4)hang (2)h(i/)m_ (hang4 him2 行險), to follow dangerous pursuits; _(4)hang (1)ping_ (hang4 bing1 行兵), to direct troops; _(4)hang (4)wai_ (hang4 wai4 行為), conduct, manner of acting; _(4)hang ling(6)_ (hang4 ling6 行令) to send an order; _~~(4)hang~~ (4)h(a/)ng (5)h(a/) ~~(2)ch(e/)~~ ch(e/)(3)_ (haang4 haa5 ze3 行吓嗻), wait, or do; a little presently; _(4)hang (1)sh(u_ (hang4 syu1 行書), to write a running hand~~,~~; _~~(4)hang~~ (4)h(a/)ng (4)l(u/)i_ (haang4 leoi4 行雷), to thunder. (Page 716 #6: (4)行) Temporary, for the present; _(4)hang (4)ying_ (hang4 jing4 行營), a movable or flying camp. Read _hang(6)_ (hang6) in colloquial. Tense, taut, drawn tight, as a drum or umbrella. Williams' _(4)hang_ (hang4) has been normalised to vernacular _(4)h(a/)ng_ (haang4) where appropriate. Williams' 行路: Or more generally, to walk. To be distinguished run 走, to run. Williams' 行刑: Better rendered "to carry out punishment". Williams' 行兵: Also _(4)h(a/)ng (1)ping_ (haang4 bing1), to move a pawn (in Chinese Chess). Williams' 行吓嗻: Corrected _(2)ch(e/)_ (ze2) to _ch(e/)(3)_ (ze3). In modern Cantonese the final particle would be 啫 ze1 instead of the (now) dated 嗻 ze3. Williams' "Read ... in colloquial": The reading _hang(6)_ (hang6) for Cantonese "taut" appears to be obsolete. The 144th radical (U+2F8F ⾏ "walk-enclosure"). 【行-level】 (haeng) (_verb-like_) to walk, to move, (_met._) journey (_verb-like_) to perform, to enact (_noun-like_) walk-way (_noun-like_) (_met._) element Cantonese retains the classical distinction between 行 "walk" and 走 "run". 【行-walk】 (haang4) To walk. 行得慢 (haang4 dak1 maan6): "To walk slowly." 行得正企得正 (haang4 dak1 zeng3 kei5 dak1 zeng3): "He walks properly and stands properly" (i.e. he is beyond reproach). To move, to go. 行得慢 (haang4 dak1 maan6): "To move slowly" (of a vehicle). 好行喇 (hou2 haang4 laa3): "We'd better make a move". 【行街】 (haang4 gaai1) To walk around in the street (e.g. on a date). (_adjective_) Takeaway. 【行行企企】 (haang4 haang4 kei5 kei5) To stand around with little to do. (Literally, "walk walk stand stand".) 【行路】 (haang4 lou6) To walk. 行路去 (haang4 lou6 heoi3): "Go by walking" (as opposed to driving). 【行-taut】 (hang4) Taut. 唔夠行 (m4 gau3 hang4): "Not taut enough." 扯行啲 (ce2 hang4 di1): "Pull it tauter." Maximally. 踹行油 (jaai2 hang4 jau4-2): "Stepping fully on the accelerator" (i.e. flooring it). 開行冷氣 (hoi1 hang4 laang5 hei3): "Running air-con at maximum." The spelling 行 for hang4 meaning "taut" or "maximally" is arbitrary.

hang6.text: U+884C (F2.32 行) 德行又身之所行爲也 (Page 74 #4: 行(6)) Actions, conduct (Kangxi: 行迹也, 德行內外在心爲德施之爲行); _(2)pan hang(6)_ (ban2 hang6 品行) disposition, character; _tak(7) hang(6)_ (dak1 hang6 德行) virtue, good works; _t(o\)(6) hang(6) (1)sham_ (dou6 hang6 sam1 道行深), able, experienced, learned; _sun(3) hang(6)_ (seon3 hang6 信行) honest; _(2)t(un hang(6)_ (dyun2 hang6 短行) curt, snappish. 【行-departing】 (haengH) (_noun-like_) conduct

hai1.text: U+95AA 𡚦 【閪】 (hai1) (_vulgar_) The vulva. (_vulgar_) The vagina. **One of the five profanities censored on Hong Kong television.** More or less equivalent to English "cunt". For non-literal senses, see the Wiktionary entry for 閪. The spelling 閪 is arbitrary.

hai2.text: U+55BA (Page 68 #11: (2)喺) To be at, to be in; ~~is;~~ well so, no more; a final particle denoting that there is no more to be said or done; _(5)n(i/) chung(6) (2)hai ~~ko(3)~~ (2)ko ch(')(u(3)_ (nei5 zung6 hai2 go2 cyu3 你重喺嗰處) do you still stay there? _(2)hai ~~ch(u(3)~~ ch(')(u(3) (4)'m (2)hai_ (hai2 cyu3 m4 hai2 喺處唔喺), is it there? is he in? _(2)hai (1)p(i/)n ch(')(u(3) (4)loi_ (hai2 bin1 cyu3 loi4 喺邊處來), where do you come from? _(2)k(o\)m y(e/)ung(6) (2)hai l(e/)(3)_ (gam2 joeng6-2 hai2 le3 噉樣喺唎) that will do, no more; _(2)hai lok(8)_ (hai2 lok3 喺咯) that's the fact, there!---an expression of surprise. Williams' "is": This sense is incorrect. Williams' "well so, no more", "a final particle ...": These senses are very dated. Williams' 你重喺嗰處: Changed _ko(3)_ (go3) to modern _(2)ko_ (go2). Williams' 喺處唔喺: Corrected _ch(u(3)_ (zyu3) to _ch(')(u(3)_ (cyu3). This is dated syntax. In modern Cantonese, it would be 喺唔喺處, with only the verb hugging the negative. 【喺】 (hai2) To be at, to be in. 我喺屋企 (ngo5 hai2 uk1 kei2): "I'm at home." 我喺街 (ngo5 hai2 gaai1): "I'm in the street" (i.e. out and about). At, in. 喺澳洲 (hai2 ou3 zau1): "In Australia." 【喺度】 (hai2 dou6) To be here. 唔喺度 (m4 hai2 dou6): "It isn't here." 唔喺度 (m4 hai2 dou6): "He isn't here" (sometimes used euphemistically to indicate that someone has died). To be in the process of. 喺度打機 (hai2 dou6 daa2 gei1): "Playing video games." The spelling 喺 is arbitrary (but well established).

hai4.text: U+516E (F1.29 兮) 語詞 (Page 68 #9: (4)兮) A poetical word used as an exclamation (Kangxi: 語有所稽也 etc.) ~~of admiration or interrogation, according as it is~~ in the middle or end of a sentence; ah! 【兮】 (hej) (_speech-assist_)

U+595A 㜎 (for female "slave" sense) (F1.29 奚) 何也 (Page 68 #7: (4)奚) Why, how? (Kangxi: 疑問辭) a page to an officer, a waiting-maid (Kangxi: 隷役也, 奚猶今官婢通作㜎傒). A surname (Kangxi: 姓). 【奚】 (hej) (_adverb-like_) what, why (_noun-like_) slave

U+5FAF 傒 蹊 hai5 (alternative per 《廣韻》胡禮切) (F1.29 徯) 待也 (Page 68 #8: (4)徯) To wait for (Kangxi: 待也), to hope (Kangxi: 有所望也); (Page 716 #13: (1)蹊) Same as 徯 _(4)hai_ (hai4), (...). 【徯】 (hej, hejX) (_verb-like_) to await

U+8E4A 傒 徯 kai1 (per Fan Wan) (F1.28 蹊 _(1)K(')ai_ (kai1)) 小路 (Page 68 #8: (4)徯) a narrow pathway (Kangxi 徯: 與蹊通); _(4)hai king(3)_ (hai4 ging3 徯徑) a footpath (Kangxi 徯: 徯徑細小狹路也). (Page 120 #5: (1)蹊 _(1)K(')ai_ (kai1); here normalised to _(4)Hai_ (hai4)) A foot or bridle-path (Kangxi: 徑道也, 步所用道曰蹊), a narrow pathway; to penetrate through byways, to go where no road is (Kangxi: 徑也). ~~Often read _(1)hai_ (hai1).~~ Williams' "Often read ...": The reading _(1)hai_ (hai1) is very dubious. 【蹊】 (hej) (_noun-like_) footpath (_verb-like_) to path

U+9F37 (F1.29 鼷) 小鼠春秋鼷鼠食郊牛角 (Page 68 #10: (4)鼷) A small meadow mouse, whose bite is considered poisonous (Kangxi: 小鼠也, 螫毒食人及鳥獸皆不痛今之甘口鼠也, etc.). Fan Wan entry: Normalised headword ⿺⿱白⿵𠘨氺奚 to 鼷, fixed missing dot in ⿱白⿵𠘨氺 then normalised to 鼠, and normalised ⿱白⿵𠘨⿻二丨 to 鼠. 【鼷】 (hej) (_noun-like_) small-mouse

hai6.text: U+4FC2 系 gai3 (per 《廣韻》古詣切) (F1.34 係) 戀也又聯也是也 (Page 68 #12: 係(6)) The substantive verb; to be, am, is; to connect, to succeed to, to relate to (Kangxi: 係繼也); _(1)p(i/)n hai(6)_ (bin1 hai6 邊係) not at all so; _hai(6) (4)'m hai(6)_ (hai6 m4 hai6 係唔係) is it so? _(1)h(a/)n hai(6)_ (haan1 hai6 ？係) was it not so? _hai(6) ~~lok(9)~~ lok(8)_ (hai6 lok3 係咯) yes; _(4)'m hai(6)_ (m4 hai6 唔係) no; _(2)t(i/)m hai(6)_ (dim2 hai6 點係) how will it be? _(2)tsung hai(6) (2)k(o\)m_ (zung2 hai6 gam2 總係噉), it is all just so; _tsau(6) hai(6) (5)k(')(u_ (zau6 hai6 keoi5 就係佢), it is just him; _hai(6) ~~(4)mo~~ (1)mo_ (hai6 mo1 係麼), is it not so? _hai(6) (1)t(o\) (5)yau_ (hai6 dou1 jau5 係都有), everything is here, you have all sorts; _(2)kwo (4)(i/)n hai(6)_ (gwo2 jin4 hai6 果然係) it is the case~~, you have all sorts~~; _ch(i/)(3) hai(6)_ (zi3 hai6 至係) ~~at the time,~~ that is better. The reading _hai(6)_ (hai6) is not unattested; 《集韻》 has the reading 胡計切, explained 説文絜束也通作結. Fan Wan entry: Corrected malformed 聯. Williams' 係咯: Corrected _lok(9)_ (lok6) to _lok(8)_ (lok3). Better rendered "it is". Williams' 唔係: Better rendered "it isn't". Williams' 係麼: Corrected _(4)mo_ (mo4) to _(1)mo_ (mo1). To tie, to bind (Kangxi: 係縛也). 【係】 (kejH) (_verb-like_) to tie, to bind (_verb-like_) (_met._) to connect, to relate (to) 【係】 (hai6) (_copula_) To be. 係 (hai6): "It is." 唔係 (m4 hai6): "It isn't." 係咪 (hai6 mai6): "Is it or isn't it?" 係咪啊 (hai6 mai6 aa3): "Is it or isn't it?" (i.e. am I not right?) 係人都想 (hai6 jan4 dou1 soeng2): "All that are human want to" (i.e. everyone wants to). 係得咁多 (hai6 dak1 gam3 do1): "There is only that much." 係定啦 (hai6 ding6-2 laa1): "It certainly is!" 又係佢 (jau6 hai6 keoi5): "It is him again." 即係話 (zik1 hai6 waa6): "That is to say." 【係都】 (hai6 dou1) To emphatically insist upon (an unacceptable action). (Literally, "even whatever be". Here, 係 is a subjunctive copula.) 係都要去 (hai6 dou1 jiu3 heoi3): "*Have* to go to it." 係都唔聽 (hai6 dou1 m4 teng1): "He just *has* to not listen to me." 【係噉】 (hai6 gam2) Incessantly. (Literally, "in such manner as being". This term is typically spoken with a subtle emphasis or lingering on 係, so as to distinguish it from conjunctive 係噉 "being so" or "then".) 係噉鬧 (hai6 gam2 naau6): "Incessantly scolding." 係噉嘈 (hai6 gam2 cou4): "Incessantly making noise." 【係咪】 (hai6 mai6) Short for 係唔係, "is it or isn't it". The copulative sense of 係 is not exclusive to Cantonese. It appears in formal writing, for example: In numerous entries of 《集韻考正》, typically in the stock comment 案此係新坿字, "Note. This is a New Annex character", made against characters not in the original 《說文》. In Yu Ying-shih's graduation certificate, which begins with 學生余英時係安徽省市潛山縣人. However, it is mainly Cantonese and Hakka that use it in everyday speech, leading to the (incorrect) perception that it is informal.

U+7CFB (F1.34 系) 世系緒也繼也 (Page 68 #13: 系(6)) To connect, to tie (Kangxi: 繫也, 相連繫也); to continue (Kangxi: 系繼也); a succession (Kangxi: 系者胤也); _shai(3) hai(6)_ (sai3 hai6 世系) a genealogy, a family record; _(1)s(e/)ung hai(6)_ (soeng1 hai6 相系) continuous. (Intrinsically, and otherwise, an alternative form of 繫. **See 繫 hai6 for the canonical entry.**) Fan Wan entry: Corrected malformed 繼. A system. An educational department or faculty. 【系】 (hejH) (_verb-like_) to connect (_noun-like_) (_met._) lineage

U+7E6B 係 傒 系 gai3 (per 《廣韻》古詣切 for "tie/bind" sense) (F1.31 繫 _Kai(3)_ (gai3)) 結也束縛也 (F1.34 繫) 因繫羈繫又音計 (Page 68 #14: 繫(6)) To tie, to bind (Kangxi: 約束也); ~~to continue;~~ attached to (Kangxi: 繫辭者聖人繫屬此辭于卦爻之下), to think of; to retain, to hold; _hai(6) (1)chau_ (hai6 zau1 繫舟), to fasten a boat; _hai(6) ~~(5)lui~~ lui(6)_ (hai6 leoi6 繫累), to implicate. (Page 120 #1: 繫(3) _Kai(3)_ (gai3)) Usually read _~~hai(3)~~ hai(6)_ (hai6), to tie; ~~to pertain to, to follow in consequence of.~~ Fan Wan entry: Fixed incomplete stroke in (first) headword 繫, corrected malformed 羈, and fixed missing character 又. Williams' "to continue": This is a misreading of Kangxi 續也 (but an understandable one, since 續也 is a very poor way of explaining the "connect" sense). Williams' 繫累: Corrected _(5)lui_ (leoi5) to _lui(6)_ (leoi6). Williams' "Usually read ...": Corrected _hai(3)_ (hai3) to _hai(6)_ (hai6). To connect (Kangxi: 繫聯綴也). To suspend, to hang. 【繫-voiced】 (hejH) (_verb-like_) to connect (_verb-like_) to suspend, to hang, (_met._) to attach 【繫-unvoiced】 (kejH) (_verb-like_) to tie, to bind

hak1.text: U+514B 剋 勀 勊 尅 haak1 (longer syllable) (F2.33 克) 能也勝也又聚斂曰掊克 (Page 69 #13: 克(7)) To sustain, to carry (Kangxi: 肩也), adequate to (Kangxi: 肩任也任者又負荷之名也能勝此物謂之克也, 克能也); superior to; to subdue, to conquer (Kangxi: 勝也); _hak(7) chai(3)_ (hak1 zai3 克制) to order, to make one obey; _hak(7) (2)f(u/)_ (hak1 fu2 克苦), hurried, oppressed; _fat(7) hak(7) (1)shing yam(6)_ (fat1 hak1 sing1 jam6 弗克勝任) inadequate for the place; _hak(7) (1)tong_ (hak1 dong1 克當), to sustain, fit for; _hak(7) (2)k(i/)_ (hak1 gei2 克己), to do what you ask others, self-government. (Page 70 #4: 尅(7) _H(a/)k(7)_ (haak1); here normalised to 克 _Hak(7)_ (hak1)) To subdue, to overcome (Kangxi 剋: 剋勝也, 謂得勝也); Fan Wan entry: Fixed missing stroke in 能 and corrected 拮 to 掊. Williams' "to subdue, to conquer": This requires Kangxi 勝也 to be departing-tone. Williams' 克制: In modern usage, a reflexive "restrain" rather than a transitive "subdue". To subdue (oneself), to restrain (Kangxi: 勝己之私謂之克). 【克】 (khok) (_verb-like_) to sustain, to carry (_adjective-like_) capable (_verb-like_) to overcome, to vanquish (_verb-like_) to subdue

U+523B 剋 (for all senses except time-unit sense) haak1 (longer syllable) kaak1 (lazy elision in 即刻) (F2.33 刻) 時刻刋刻鏤也刺也 (Page 70 #3: 刻(7) _H(a/)k(7)_ (haak1); here normalised to _Hak(7)_ (hak1)) To carve (Kangxi: 鏤也), to chisel, to sculpture; ~~a~~ to cut (Kangxi: 割也); griping (Kangxi: 一曰痛也)~~, close~~; fifteen minutes, a little while (Kangxi: 刻漏也 etc.); _~~h(a/)k(7)~~ hak(7) tsz'(6)_ (hak1 zi6 刻字) to cut characters; _~~h(a/)k(7)~~ hak(7) (2)p(a/)n_ (hak1 baan2 刻版), to cut blocks; _h(a/)n(6) ~~h(a/)k(7)~~ hak(7)_ (haan6 hak1 限刻) a limit, a set time; _~~h(a/)k(7)~~ hak(7) kwat(7) (5)ming (1)sam_ (hak1 gwat1 ming5 sam1 刻骨銘心), graven on the bones and inscribed in the heart; _~~h(a/)k(7)~~ hak(7) h(a/)(6)_ (hak1 haa6) presently; _~~h(a/)k(7)~~ hak(7) yat(9)_ (hak1 jat6 刻日) a set day; _(4)sh(i/) ~~h(a/)k(7)~~ hak(7)_ (si4 hak1 時刻) constant, usual; _(2)shi(u/) ~~h(a/)k(7)~~ hak(7)_ (siu2 hak1 少刻) a little time. Fan Wan entry: Corrected ⿱艹⿰丩寸 to 時, corrected 利 to 刋, corrected 鏌 to 鏤, and corrected 剌 to 刺. Williams' 刻日: That is, an appointed day. To take away, to deprive (Kangxi: 剝也), to reduce. Used in 刻薄, 苛刻 (harsh) (Kangxi: 刻薄慘覈也). To injure (Kangxi: 害也). 【刻】 (khok) (_verb-like_) to engrave, to cut (_verb-like_) (_met._) to injure (_verb-like_) (_met._) to appoint (_adjective-like_) (_met._) harsh (_noun-like_) time-mark

U+524B 克 勀 勊 尅 haak1 (longer syllable) (F2.33 尅) 殺也損也又五行生尅 (Page 69 #13: 克(7); here normalised to 剋) overbearing; (Page 70 #4: 尅(7) _H(a/)k(7)_ (haak1); here normalised to 剋 _Hak(7)_ (hak1)) to repress, to exorcise; urgent (Kangxi 剋: 必也急也); _~~h(a/)k(7)~~ hak(7) sh(a/)t(8) (1)hung (4)shan_ (hak1 saat3 hung1 san4 剋煞凶神), to drive off unlucky demons; _(1)shang ~~h(a/)k(7)~~ hak(7)_ (sang1 hak1 生剋) to produce and destroy (said of the five elements); _~~h(a/)k(7)~~ hak(7) chai(3)_ (hak1 zai3 剋制) to lord it over one; _~~h(a/)k(7)~~ hak(7) (2)k(a/)m_ (hak1 gaam2 剋減), to reduce a debt or wages by force; _~~h(a/)k(7)~~ hak(7) pok(9)_ (hak1 bok6 剋薄) hardfisted, oppressive, insulting. Williams' 剋薄: Now usually spelt 刻薄. To appoint (a date) (Kangxi: 剋期約定日期也). (_astrology_) To conflict with, to be harmful to.

U+9ED1 haak1 (longer syllable) (F2.33 黑) 北方之色 (Page 69 #12: 黑(7)) Black (Kangxi: 火所熏之色也, 北方隂色), sooty; dark, obscure (Kangxi: 黑晦也如晦冥時色也); cloudy, dull; wicked; _hak(7) shik(7)_ (hak1 sik1 黑色) black color; _hak(7) (o\)m(3)_ (hak1 am3 黑暗) dark, not well lighted; _hak(7) (1)sam_ (hak1 sam1 黑心), villainous; _hak(7) fo(3)_ (hak1 fo3 黑貨) opium; _hak(7) p(a/)k(9) (4)n(a/)n (1)fan_ (hak1 baak6 naan4 fan1 黑白難分), good and bad are not easily distinguished; _(1)kam (5)m(a/)n hak(7)_ (gam1 maan5-1 hak1 今晚黑) to-night. Williams' 黑貨: More generally, contraband. The 203rd radical (U+2FCA ⿊ "black"). 【黑】 (xok) (_adjective-like_) black 【黑麻麻】 (hak1 maa4-1 maa4-1) Very dark (of viewing conditions). 【黑𠵼𠵼】 (hak1 mang1 mang1) Very dark (of viewing conditions, or in colour). 【黑咪𠵼】 (hak1 mi1 mang1) Synonym of 黑𠵼𠵼. 【黑屎竻掘】 (hak1 si2 lak6 gwak6) Black or very dark in colour (when undesirable). The spellings 𠵼𠵼 for mang1 mang1, 咪𠵼 for mi1 mang1, and 竻掘 for lak6 gwak6 are arbitrary; these are likely phonetic suffixes.

han2.text: U+58BE 豤 垦 (Mainland simplified) (F1.83 墾) 開墾又治也 (Page 71 #8: (2)墾) To open new land (Kangxi: 一曰開田用力反土也), to plough, to cultivate (Kangxi: 力治也); to injure (Kangxi: 傷也如鉏墾之傷物也); ~~energetic;~~ _(1)hoi (2)han_ (hoi1 han2 開墾), to clear land; _(2)han t(i/)(6)_ (han2 dei6 墾地) new land; _(2)han chung(3)_ (han2 zung3 墾種) to plough and sow. Fan Wan entry: Corrected 冶 to 治. Williams' "to injure": Better rendered "to damage". Williams' "energetic": This is a misreading of 力 in the various Kangxi definitions. 【墾】 (khonX) (_verb-like_) to plough up, to open up (_verb-like_) (_met._) to damage

U+5F88 佷 (for "disobey" sense) 狠 han5 (per 《廣韻》胡墾切) (F1.83 狠) 强狠不聽從也 (Page 71 #9: (2)很(2)狠) disobedient, perverse (Kangxi 很: 不聽從也, 很違也); quarrelsome (Kangxi 很: 諍訟也, 很鬩也謂爭訟也), intractable; sign of the superlative; very, much; _(1)to tak(7) (2)han_ (do1 dak1 han2 多得很), very many; _(2)han w(a/)i(6)_ (han2 waai6 很壞) very bad. Williams does not provide separate entries for 很 and 狠. I have split things up accordingly. Williams' "perverse": Meaning "contrary". Williams' "intractable": Meaning "obstinate". Williams' 多得很: Fixed missing tone marker _(2)_ for 很. 【很】 (honX) (_verb-like_) to disobey (_verb-like_) to quarrel

U+61C7 豤 貇 頎 恳 (Mainland simplified) (F1.83 懇) 情切也 (F1.83 𢢽) 同上 (Page 71 #7: (2)懇) To request, to beg, to ask as a favor; importunate, truly, earnestly (Kangxi: 悃也, 誠也, 信也, 或作貇, 款誠之意); _(2)han (4)k(')au_ (han2 kau4 懇求), to intreat; _(2)han k(')ap(7)_ (han2 kap1 懇給) ask to give; _(2)han (1)yan_ (han2 jan1 懇恩), to ask a kindness. Kangxi 亦作頎《禮檀弓》頎乎其至也《註》頎音懇惻隱之貌 is difficult to make sense of. On the surface, this appears to define 頎 (and 懇) as "pitying". But that does not make sense; the context is 稽顙而後拜頎乎其至也, in which 頎乎其至也 describes a mourner kowtowing them bowing to a visitor. The mourner can hardly be "pitying" the visitor. The only way out of this conundrum is if 惻隱之貌 is "pitiable", but that interpretation is still not very satisfactory. 【懇】 (khonX) (_adjective-like_) sincere

U+72E0 很 (F1.83 狠) 强狠不聽從也 (Page 71 #9: (2)很(2)狠) revengeful, vicious, ruthless; _mat(7) (5)n(i/) ~~(2)k(o\)m~~ k(o\)m(3) (2)han (1)sam_ (mat1 nei5 gam3 han2 sam1 乜你咁狠心), how harsh you are! _f(a/)t(8) (2)han_ (faat3 han2 發狠), very angry; Williams does not provide separate entries for 很 and 狠. I have split things up accordingly. Williams' 乜你咁狠心: Corrected _(2)k(o\)m_ (gam2) to _k(o\)m(3)_ (gam3).
U+8C64 狠 Probably cognate with 齦. To gnaw like a pig (Kangxi: 齧也, 豕齧地, 豕食貌, 齒深入物也).
U+9F66 龈 (Mainland simplified) Probably cognate with 豤. To gnaw (Kangxi: 齧也).

han4.text: U+75D5 han4-2 (vernacular rising-tone noun for line-shaped "mark" sense and rising second in vernacular 痕痕地) (F1.82 痕) 癢痕又水痕 (Page 71 #6: (4)痕) A scar, a cicatrix (Kangxi: 胝瘢也, 瘢痕也); a mark, trace, or line left (Kangxi: 凡物有迹者皆曰痕 etc.); an itching; _lui(6) (4)han_ (leoi6 han4 淚痕), marks of tears; _(2)shui (4)han_ (seoi2 han4 水痕), a stain from water; _(2)h(o\) (4)han_ (hou2 han4 好痕), very itchy; _(4)han tsik(7)_ (han4 zik1 痕跡) a trace, a flaw in glass. Fan Wan entry: Corrected malformed 癢. 【痕】 (hon) (_noun-like_) scar 【痕】 (han4) Itchy. 痕癢 (han4 joeng5): "Itchiness." 𢯎痕 (ngaau1 han4): "Scratch an itch." 痕痕地 (han4 han4-2 dei6-2): "A bit itchy." 屎窟痕 (si2 fat1 han4): "His arse must have been itchy" (i.e. he had no good reason to do that). The spelling 痕 is arbitrary (but well established).

han6.text: U+6068 (F1.85 恨) 忿恨怒恨 (Page 71 #10: 恨(6)) Indignation, resentment, dislike; hatred (Kangxi: 怨也), spite; to regret, to feel sorry (Kangxi: 悔恨也); vexed, sorry; _han(6) n(o\)(6)_ (han6 nou6 恨怒) to hate; _(2)ho han(6)_ (ho2 han6 可恨) detestable, odious; _s(ut(8) han(6)_ (syut3 han6 雪恨) gratified revenge; _han(6) pat(7) tak(7)_ (han6 bat1 dak1 恨不得) would that! O for! _(4)m(o\) (4)yan han(6)_ (mou4 jan4 han6 無人恨) unregretted; _tak(7) (4)yan han(6)_ (dak1 jan4 han6 得人恨) to get men's ill will. 【恨】 (honH) (_verb-like_) to detest, to hate (_verb-like_) to regret 【恨】 (han6) To yearn for, to long for. 恨生仔 (han6 saang1 zai2): "Yearn to have kids." 恨退休 (han6 teoi3 jau1): "Long for retirement." 唔使恨喇 (m4 sai2 han6 la3): "You needn't bother longing for it" (i.e. you probably won't get it).

hang1.text: U+4EA8 享 亯 (F2.29 亨) 通也 (Page 72 #12: (1)亨) To penetrate or pervade (Kangxi: 通也); successful; _(1)hang (1)k(')(u_ (hang1 keoi1 亨區), a quiet street, an eligible street. 【亨】 (xaeng) (_adjective-like_) penetrating

U+54FC (Page 72 #13: (1)哼) Frightened, an antipathy to (Kangxi: 嗆哼愚怯貌); a local word applied to smells, lothsome. Commonly used to spell the interjection hm1 or hng1 (equivalent to English hmph!). Williams' "a local word applied to smells": Eitel (1877) gives the example 臭哼哼 _ch(')au(3) (1)hang (1)hang_ (cau3 hang1 hang1), explained "a nasty smell". To hum.

U+727C hang4 (alternative per 《廣韻》戸耕切 for "shinbone" sense) (F2.29 牼) 牛膝下骨又人名宋牼 (Page 72 #16: (1)牼) The shank bone of an ox (Kangxi: 牛膝下骨也). A man, Sung(3) (1)Hang (sung3 hang1 宋牼), in the time of Mencius (Kangxi: 人名 etc.). Fan Wan entry: Corrected malformed 膝.

U+785C 硻 䃘 踁 (for "rockheaded" sense) 硁 (Mainland simplified) (F2.29 硜) 石堅確聲 (Page 72 #15: (1)硜) The jingling of stones, striking hard stones together (Kangxi: 石聲). Probably cognate with 鏗. Rockheaded, hardheaded (Kangxi: 硜硜小人貌). 【硜】 (kheang) (_onomatopoeia_) clang, (_met._) clack (_adjective-like_) (_met._) rockheaded
U+811D 亨 (Page 716 #5: (1)脝) A puffed belly (Kangxi: 膨脝脹也, 膨脝腹滿貌); _(4)p(')(a/)ng (1)hang_ (paang4 hang1 膨脝), a swelled belly, one distended by wind.

U+93D7 硻 銵 鍞 铿 (Mainland simplified) (F2.29 鏗) 鏗鏘玉聲又瑟聲 (Page 72 #14: (1)鏗) To strike against (Kangxi: 撞也) as sounding glasses or metals, a ringing or metallic sound (Kangxi: 鏗鏘金石聲, 或作鍞銵); _(1)hang (1)ts(')(e/)ung_ (hang1 coeng1 鏗鏘), jingling of bangles or tamborines. Probably cognate with 硜. (_onomatopoeia_) The sound of a zither being played (Kangxi: 琴聲). 【鏗】 (kheang) (_onomatopoeia_) clang

hang2.text: U+80AF 肎 肻 hoi2 (alternative per 《集韻》許亥切 for "flesh attached to bone" sense) (F2.31 肯) 允也許也 (Page 73 #7: (2)肯) ~~The attachment of the muscles~~ Flesh attached to bone (Kangxi: 著骨肉也); to assent, willing, acquiescing (Kangxi: 肯可也); to permit; _(2)hang (4)'m (2)hang_ (hang2 m4 hang2 肯唔肯), will you or not? _(4)'m (2)hang_ (m4 hang2 唔肯), I will not! _(5)wan (2)hang_ (wan5 hang2 允肯), to permit. 【肯】 (khongX) (_noun-like_) flesh attached to bone (_verb-like_) to be willing

hang4.text: U+6046 㔰 恒 (F2.30 恆) 常也久也 (F2.30 ？) 同上 (Page 73 #6: (4)恒; here normalised to 恆) Constant, regular, perpetual (Kangxi 恆: 常也, 恆久也), according to rule (Kangxi 恆: 恆故也必因循故法也); to continue of the same mind, persevering; _(4)hang (4)sh(e/)ung_ (hang4 soeng4 恆常), accustomed to; _(4)hang (1)sam_ (hang4 sam1 恆心), constant; _(4)hang (2)yan_ (hang4 jan2 恆忍), patient; _(4)hang (2)ch(')(a/)n_ (hang4 caan2 恆產), enduring possessions; _(4)Hang (4)ho (1)sh(a/) sh(o\)(3)_ (hang4 ho4 saa1 sou3 恆河沙數) like the sands of the Ganges; _(4)Hang (1)sh(a/)n_ (hang4 saan1 恆山), a mountain in the west of Chihl(i/) (直隸) (Kangxi 恆: 山名). Fan Wan entry: The second form of the headword is 恆 but with one less dot in the component 亙. Ordinary. 【恆-level】 (hong) (_adjective-like_) persistent, (_met._) established

U+73E9 衡 (F2.30 珩) 白玉曰珩 (Page 73 #2: (4)珩) ~~An~~ The gem on an ornamented clasp~~, a gem which has a play of colors, worn on the person~~ (Kangxi: 佩上玉也 etc., 通作衡). 【珩】 (haeng) (_noun-like_) girdle-gem

U+8605 𧄇 衡 (F2.30 蘅) 香草 (Page 73 #4: (4)𧄇; here normalised to 蘅) A fragrant plant like mallows (Kangxi 蘅: 香草也 etc.); _t(o\)(6) (4)hang_ (dou6 hang4 杜蘅), sweet vernal-grass (Kangxi 蘅: 杜衡葉似葵形如馬蹄故俗云馬蹄香). (?) Williams' 杜蘅: Strictly, _Asarum forbesii_.

U+8861 𢖍 (F2.30 衡) 平也論也車鈪也又音橫 (Page 73 #3: (4)𢖍; here normalised to 衡) A yoke or strap on the head of cattle (Kangxi 衡: 楅衡所以楅持牛使不得抵觸也); the space under the eyebrows (Kangxi 衡: 眉目之閒也); a balance, or thing to weigh with (Kangxi 衡: 衡平也所以任權而均物平輕重也); a balustrade (Kangxi 衡: 樓殿邊欄楯也); to weigh; transverse (Kangxi 衡: 橫也); adjusted, compared; _(4)hang (4)l(e/)ung_ (hang4 loeng4 衡量), to measure; _(4)hang (4)p(')ing_ (hang4 ping4 衡平), a pair of scales; _yuk(9) (4)hang_ (juk6 hang4 玉衡), an armillary sphere (Kangxi 衡: 璣衡王者正天文之器可運轉者, 衡謂渾天儀也). Fan Wan entry: Corrected 黃 to 橫. Williams' 衡量: Also read _(4)hang l(e/)ung(6)_ (hang4 loeng6). Verb-like 量 can be departing (e.g. in 量入, 量力). A dragon-head ladle handle (Kangxi: 勺柄龍頭也). 【衡】 (haeng) (_noun-like_) yoke, crosspiece, crossbeam (_noun-like_) steelyard-beam, (_met._) balance

hang6.text: U+5016 幸 (Mainland simplified) (F2.32 幸) 慶幸不當得而得與不可免而免皆曰幸又冀望也得也愛也又天子車駕所至曰幸 (F2.32 倖) 徼倖 (Page 74 #1: 倖(6)) Fan Wan entry: Fixed missing stroke ㇖ in 慶, and fixed missing final stroke in 當.
U+5A5E 倖 悻 (Page 73 #8: (2)悻 _(2)Hang_ (hang2); here corrected to _Hang(6)_ (hang6) and normalised to 婞) quarrelsome, pertinacious (Kangxi 婞: 同悻, 很也). 【婞】 (hengX) (_adjective-like_) stubborn

U+5E78 倖 (for "fortunate" and "favour" senses) 婞 (for "favour" sense) (F2.32 幸) 慶幸不當得而得與不可免而免皆曰幸又冀望也得也愛也又天子車駕所至曰幸 (F2.32 倖) 徼倖 (Page 73 #9: 幸(6)) Fortunate, lucky (Kangxi: 吉而免凶也 etc.); blessed; happily; an emperor reaching or tarrying in a place (Kangxi: 幸天子所至也); to hope, to wait or long for (Kangxi: 冀也, 幸覬也); lucky in getting, to rejoice; to love (Kangxi: 幸御所親愛也), pleased; _hang(6) tak(7)_ (hang6 dak1 幸得) to succeed pleasantly; _sh(i/)(6) hang(6)_ (si6 hang6 是幸) is well, will be pleased---a phrase used in a bill; _(1)k(a/) (4)m(u/)n pat(7) hang(6)_ (gaa1 mun4 bat1 hang6 家門不幸) domestic affliction, family trouble; _pat(7) hang(6) (1)chung (1)ch(i/) hang(6)_ (bat1 hang6 zung1 zi1 hang6 不幸中之幸) fortunate in the midst of disaster. (Page 74 #1: 倖(6)) To obtain or avoid without merit or right (Kangxi 幸: 非分而得曰幸, 非所當得而得與不可免而免曰幸); _hang(6) (5)m(i/)n_ (hang6 min5 倖免), fortunately escaped; _(1)hi(u/) hang(6)_ (hiu1 hang6 僥倖) very fortunate. Fan Wan entry: Fixed missing stroke ㇖ in 慶, and fixed missing final stroke in 當. Williams' "to love": Better rendered "to favour". 【幸】 (heangX) (_noun-like_) luck, fortune (_verb-like_) to feel glad at

U+60BB 𢙼 hang2 (per Fan Wan) hang5 (not recast to departing) (F2.31 悻 _(2)Hang_ (hang2)) 怨也怒也恨也 (Page 73 #8: (2)悻 _(2)Hang_ (hang2); here normalised to _Hang(6)_ (hang6)) _~~(2)Hang (2)hang~~ Hang(6) hang(6)_ (hang6 hang6), anger, hatred (Kangxi: 悻悻很怒也); great displeasure, vexed; 【悻】 (hengX) (_adjective-like_) wrathful

U+674F (F2.32 杏) 果名 (Page 74 #2: 杏(6)) A kind of plum (Kangxi: 果名 etc.); _hang(6) (4)yan_ (hang6 jan4 杏仁), almonds; _(4)ngan hang(6)_ (ngan4 hang6 銀杏) nuts of the Salisburia adiantifolia; _hang(6) (4)m(u/)i_ (hang6 mui4 杏梅), a sort of apricot, ripe in June. Williams' "A kind of plum": Specifically, the apricot. Williams' 銀杏: Commonly called ginkgo (or gingko) via Japanese. 【杏】 (haengX) (_noun-like_) apricot

U+8347 莕 䓷 (F2.32 荇) 菜名 (Page 74 #3: 荇(6)) An aquatic vegetable with a reddish leaf (Kangxi: 接余也 etc.); not found in Canton. Specifically, _Nymphoides peltata_, or the fringed water-lily. 【荇】 (haengX) (_noun-like_) water-fringe

he1.text: U+550F (Page 78 #5: _(1)H(e/)_ (he1) exemplified; here assigned to 唏)

hei1.text: U+550F he1 (by strict analogy with Williams) (Page 78 #5: _(1)H(e/)_ (he1) exemplified; here assigned to 唏 and hypothesised to correspond to modern hei1) A colloquial exclamation, expressing disapproval; _(1)h(e/) (4)'m (2)h(o\) ~~t(')au(3)~~ tau(3)_ (hei1, m4 hou2 dau3 唏唔好鬥) do n't touch it! Strict analogy with Williams' _(1)h(e/)_ results in the modern reading he1 hɛː. However, because Williams' _(1)h(e/)_ was likely sounded *heɪ (based on his description of the final _(e/)_), I hypothesise here that _(1)h(e/)_ actually corresponds to the modern interjection hei1, which is sounded hei. Williams' 唏唔好鬥: Corrected _t(')au(3)_ (tau3) to _tau(3)_ (dau3).

he3.text: U+20EAA 【𠺪】 (he3) To stuff around, to waste time being unproductive. 𠺪半個鐘 (he3 bun3 go3 zung1): "Stuff around for half an hour." To do without due care or effort, to treat casually. Commonly spelt hea. The spelling 𠺪 is arbitrary.

kak1.text: U+63E2 喀 (Cantonese) (Page 718 #4: _K(')ak(7)_ (kak1) exemplified; here assigned to 揢) A colloquial word. Uneven, interrupted; _lak(7) k(')ak(7)_ (lak1 kak1 肋揢) difficult, not smooth; _l(o\)(6) (2)h(o\) lak(7) k(')ak(7)_ (lou6 hou2 lak1 kak1 路好肋揢) the road is very rough; _(2)kong tak(7) lak(7) lak(7) k(')ak(7) k(')ak(7)_ (gong2 dak1 lak1 lak1 kak1 kak1 講得肋肋揢揢) to stammer, to hesitate. 【肋揢】 (lak1 kak1) Unsmooth, stuttering. The spelling 肋揢 is arbitrary. Wiktionary as of 2026-05-31 suggests 犖确 "rocky/uneven" (whose expected reading is lok6 hok6) as a possible etymology. On the other hand, I am more inclined to believe that 揢 kak1 is cognate with 撠 kik1 (TODO).

zaa1.text: U+4E4B za1 (shorter syllable) 【之嘛】 (za1 maa3) A final particle of limitation, especially used defensively. 講笑之嘛 (gong2 siu3 za1 maa3): "Just kidding!" 等兩日之嘛 (dang2 loeng5 jat6 za1 maa3): "It's just a two-day wait."
